* By contrast, demurrage money would lose value even if prices are falling, so it can increase circulation and end recessions.

If money continues to lose purchasing power (even at a slow rate), then people will use it sooner rather than later.<ref name="bozhya-volya">{{cite web |url=https://wp.hse.ru/data/2019/01/18/1148372735/207EC2019.pdf |title=Why Should Money Lose Value With Time: Boosting Economy in the Era of E-Money |last1=Bozhya-Volya |first1=Roman N. |last2=Rybak |first2=Alina S. |date=18 January 2019 |website=Higher School of Economics |publisher=National Research University Higher School of Economics |access-date=2 May 2025 |archive-date=2 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250502174715/https://wp.hse.ru/data/2019/01/18/1148372735/207EC2019.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>
Gesell proposed that money should have a demurrage rate 5.2% per year, or 0.1% per week, but he also believed that real-world experimentation would probably be necessary to figure out the optimal rate.<ref name="NEO-part-4-chap-1"/>

In some cases, demurrage currencies have been employed as [[Notgeld|emergency currencies]], intended to keep the [[circular flow of income]] running throughout the economy during recessions and times of war, due to their faster circulation velocities.<ref name=gomez-2018/>{{rp|pp=16–17}}<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|p=8}}

=== Other differences between demurrage and inflation ===
Inflation and demurrage both tend to reduce the liquid [[saving]]s over time, but there are many crucial differences between the two.
Unlike [[Inflation (economics)|inflation]], demurrage gradually reduces only the value of currency held, not on newly issued money, money placed into a bank (from the lender's perspective), nor money that will be claimed or issued in the future.<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|pp=15–16}}
In fact, demurrage would increase the value of claims to future money like [[stock]]s and [[bond (finance)|bond]]s, since they would become a more reliable way to store [[wealth]], due to the penalty on holding [[cash]].<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|p=16}}
Inflation also increases prices across the [[consumer price index]], whereas demurrage does not.

Inflation also benefits borrowers at the expense of lenders, whereas demurrage does not.
The effect of demurrage on borrowers depends on what they do with the money.
If they spend it (either for consumption or investment), they do not bear the cost of demurrage.
If borrowers hold onto the money, they would lose due to demurrage.
People are thus strongly disincentivized to borrow demurrage money without spending it.

The rate of inflation usually fluctuates, and inflation may devalue currency in a variety of ways, so inflation is not easy to predict.<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://scholar.harvard.edu/files/stock/files/whyhasinflationbecomeharderforecast.pdf |title=Why Has U.S. Inflation Become Harder to Forecast? |last1=Stock |first1=James H. |last2=Watson |first2=Mark W. |date=February 2007 |via=Harvard University |volume=39 |issue=1 |journal=Journal of Money, Credit and Banking |publisher=Blackwell Publishing Limited |access-date=2 May 2025 |archive-date=15 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815033525/https://scholar.harvard.edu/files/stock/files/whyhasinflationbecomeharderforecast.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="mitchell-2010">{{cite web |url=http://bilbo.economicoutlook.net/blog/?p=10554 |title=Modern monetary theory and inflation |last=Mitchell |first=Bill |author-link=Bill Mitchell (economist) |date=7 July 2010 |website=William Mitchell – Modern Monetary Theory |access-date=23 May 2025 |archive-date=19 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110819235555/http://bilbo.economicoutlook.net/blog/?p=10554 |url-status=live }}</ref>
By contrast, the depreciation rate of demurrage currency would stay at a fixed rate set by the government, thus leading to a more stable and predictable economy with lower prices.<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|p=16}}

Freiwirtschaft economists theorize that demurrage currency could eliminate both inflation and deflation.
There tends to be some interest cost that is built into the goods and services that consumers tend to purchase,<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|p=4}} so if demurrage currency eliminates interest rates, then prices are less likely to increase.
Demurrage would also naturally cause the money supply to decrease, thus causing deflation.
If a central bank issues and monitors demurrage currency as Gesell originally proposed, then it could replace all the money that disappears due to demurrage by printing money at a similar rate.<ref name="dillard-1997">{{cite book |last=Dillard |first=Dudley D. |date=1997 |title=Proudhon, Gesell, and Keynes |location=St. Georgen |publisher=Angela Hackbarth Verlag |isbn=3-929741-14-8 |page=112}}</ref><ref name="baynham-2023"/>
The money printing could create just enough inflation to cancel out the natural deflation of demurrage, thus achieving an [[inflation target]] of 0% and stable prices.<ref name="sidman-lecture-6-inflation">{{cite AV media |last=Sidman |first=Josh |date=3 April 2024 |title="Silvio Gesell: Beyond Capitalism vs Socialism" Class #6 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1GjX4PCcTlU%3Ft%3D918 |time=15:18 |type=Video |language=English |publisher=Henry George School of Economics |access-date=23 May 2025 |archive-date=5 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250605010407/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1GjX4PCcTlU%3Ft%3D918 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Interest rates, lending, and borrowing ===
Some regard demurrage as a [[negative interest rate]] policy, but they have different effects. Under demurrage currency, hoarding money becomes impossible because the face-value of money depreciates regularly. This forces the circulation of money.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Bershidsky|first1=Leonid|title='Neglected Prophet' of Economics Got It Right|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/view/articles/2015-07-03/-neglected-prophet-of-economics-got-it-right|newspaper=Bloomberg|date=3 July 2015|access-date=1 June 2017|archive-date=3 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170603101912/https://www.bloomberg.com/view/articles/2015-07-03/-neglected-prophet-of-economics-got-it-right|url-status=live}}</ref> By contrast, it is possible to some extent to hoard money on negative interests, since the face value of money is constant and people can use their money as a means of saving. For example, Japan's negative interest rates drove up the sales of [[safe]]s and strongboxes.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Shen|first1=Lucinda|title=Japan's Negative Interest Rates Are Driving up Sales of Safes|url=http://fortune.com/2016/02/23/japans-negative-interest-rate-driving-up-safe-sales/|access-date=1 June 2017|work=Fortune|date=2016-02-23|archive-date=3 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170603115947/http://fortune.com/2016/02/23/japans-negative-interest-rate-driving-up-safe-sales/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Negative interest rates tend to discourage people from storing their money in banks, in order to avoid having their money depreciate in value. Thus the money cannot be relent by the banks to increase the money supply, and for this reason, it can be difficult to increase the money supply, so some aspects of monetary policy could theoretically become ineffective at low interest rates.<ref name="cleveland-fed-2008"/>
Some economists have expressed interest in demurrage currency as a way to avoid this problem and effectively turn interest rates negative.<ref name="Gesell-NPR"/><ref name="Gesell-NYT"/><ref name="cleveland-fed-2008"/>

When the medium of exchange is scarce (i.e. money is not trading hands because it is functioning as a store of value), traders will pay to rent it ([[Interest (economics)|interest]]), which acts as an impedance to trade.
In stable or deflationary environments, interest is a net transfer of wealth from debtor to creditor.
Under inflationary environments, interest is a net transfer of wealth from creditor to the debtor.
Demurrage currency aims to end both of these cases.

If the [[liquidity preference]] theory of interest rates is correct, then interest rates would disappear when money cannot be used as a long-term store of value, so demurrage money would theoretically have no interest rates.
To be clear, the total interest rate typically consists of four components: [[Risk-free rate|pure (risk-free) interest]], a risk premium, expected inflation or deflation, and administrative costs.
In this context, the intended meaning is that demurrage money would theoretically have no pure interest rates, whereas the other three components of interest would remain.
Banks would still be able to profit from loaning money under a demurrage monetary system, since they would be paid by the administrative costs component of the total interest rate.<ref name="sidman-lecture-3-interest">{{cite AV media |last=Sidman |first=Josh |date=11 March 2024 |title="Silvio Gesell: Beyond Capitalism vs Socialism" Class #3 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i2DTU5gksqA%3Ft%3D88 |time=1:28 |type=Video |language=English |publisher=Henry George School of Economics |access-date=26 May 2025 |archive-date=5 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250605010408/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i2DTU5gksqA%3Ft%3D88 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Under a demurrage monetary system, banks would be incentivized to loan money to avoid paying demurrage fees.
This new incentive would lead to a further incentive for bankers to lend demurrage money without charging [[interest rate]]s, in order to reduce the disincentives for borrowers to borrow demurrage money.<ref name="baynham-2023"/><ref name="Gesell-NPR"/>
The result would be an [[interest-free economy]].

Borrowers would also be incentivized to use the demurrage money as soon as possible before the purchasing power decreases due to demurrage.
Since demurrage money would theoretically increase the velocity of money, eliminate interest rates, and lower the [[opportunity cost]]s to borrowing [[credit]], demurrage money could theoretically lead to greater economic efficiency and prosperity.<ref name="sidman-lecture-5">{{cite AV media |last=Sidman |first=Josh |date=25 March 2024 |title="Silvio Gesell: Beyond Capitalism vs Socialism" Class #5 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2qS8ol1NNAc |type=Video |language=English |publisher=Henry George School of Economics |access-date=30 April 2025 |archive-date=5 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250605010447/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2qS8ol1NNAc |url-status=live }}</ref>

For long-term investment financing, demurrage currency affects the dynamics of [[net present value]] (NPV) calculations. Demurrage in a currency system reduces discount rates, and thus increases the present value of a long-term investment, and thus gives an incentive for such investments.<ref name="Lietaer">[[Bernard Lietaer]]: [http://www.transaction.net/money/cc/cc01.html transaction.net Community Currencies: A New Tool for the 21st Century.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100612131407/http://transaction.net/money/cc/cc01.html |date=12 June 2010 }}</ref>

=== Economic and environmental sustainability ===
Freiwirtschaft economist {{ill|Felix Fuders|de}} argues that the [[growth imperative]] of modern economies is caused by interest burdens on debt, inflation, and opportunity costs created by the existence of interest.<ref name="sidman-lecture-5-fuders">{{cite AV media |last=Sidman |first=Josh |date=25 March 2024 |title="Silvio Gesell: Beyond Capitalism vs Socialism" Class #5 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2qS8ol1NNAc%3Ft%3D2681 |time=44:41 |type=Video |language=English |publisher=Henry George School of Economics |access-date=30 April 2025 |archive-date=5 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250605010430/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2qS8ol1NNAc%3Ft%3D2681 |url-status=live }}</ref>
Fuders believes that the growth imperative has harmful environmental and social consequences.<ref name="sidman-lecture-3-fuders">{{cite AV media |last=Sidman |first=Josh |date=11 March 2024 |title="Silvio Gesell: Beyond Capitalism vs Socialism" Class #3 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i2DTU5gksqA%3Ft%3D992 |time=16:32 |type=Video |language=English |publisher=Henry George School of Economics |access-date=30 April 2025 |archive-date=5 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250605010441/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i2DTU5gksqA%3Ft%3D992 |url-status=live }}</ref>
Fuders concludes that it is impossible to meaningfully address the problem of unsustainable growth or fulfill the [[sustainable development goals]] proposed by the [[United Nations]] without completely overhauling the monetary system in favor of demurrage currency.<ref>{{cite book |last=Fuders |first=Felix |date=April 2023 |title=How to Fulfill the UN Sustainability Goals: Rethinking the Role and Concept of Money in the Light of Sustainability |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-37768-6 |location=Cham, Switzerland |publisher=Springer Nature Switzerland AG |page= |doi=10.1007/978-3-031-37768-6 |isbn=978-3-031-37767-9 |access-date=30 April 2025}}</ref>

[[Bernard Lietaer]] and {{ill|Dieter Suhr|de}} have also argued that the existence of interest has negative impacts on [[resource consumption]] and the environment.
As an example, Lietaer wrote: "When it pays more to cut a tree, sell the wood and let the proceeds earn interest than simply let the tree grow, it is predictable that "economic pressures" will be felt to cut more trees than is optimal from an ecological viewpoint. Stamp Scrip would reverse that process."<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|p=5}}<ref name="steadman-2013"/>

=== Proceeds of the system ===
In some instances, the demurrage fee is charged by some sort of central authority, and is paid into a fund. The application of this fund varies widely among both historical and proposed systems. In some cases, it is used to pay the costs of administering the tax. If the currency in question is run by the government, the demurrage fee can contribute to general [[tax revenue]].

In Gesell's proposed system, the individual owners of Freigeld would pay the demurrage fee for the stamps to the government, thus reducing the amount of other taxes that a government would have to collect.<ref name="baynham-2023"/> If individuals do not want to pay the demurrage fees, they could buy assets to store their wealth or deposit their money into a bank. The bank would become responsible for paying for the stamp fees, and the money would retain its full value from the depositor's perspective. Bank would thus be incentivized to [[loan]] the money in order to pass the holding expense onto others and avoid paying for the stamps, which would guarantee that plenty of money would be available for lending in the economy. Gesell believed that banks would loan until their interest rates eventually [[Zero interest-rate policy|fall to zero]]. Banks would collect only a small [[risk premium]] and an administration fee, without any need to adjust for inflation or deflation.<ref name="baynham-2023"/><ref name="onken-2000">{{cite journal |last1=Onken |first1=Werner |date=October 2000 |title=The Political Economy of Silvio Gesell: A Century of Activism |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3487828 |journal=American Journal of Economics and Sociology |volume=59 |issue=4 |publisher=Wiley |pages=609–622 |doi=10.1111/1536-7150.00046 |jstor=3487828 |access-date=26 April 2026 |archive-date=19 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230519100619/https://www.jstor.org/stable/3487828?seq=1 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In [[mutual credit]] systems, all positive accounts, or those over a credit threshold, are debited the demurrage fee if there is no trading (purchasing) after a certain period (e.g. a month or year after the last purchase).
The fee typically accrues to the administration account and thus adds to the common credit pool.

== Critical analysis ==
British economist [[John Maynard Keynes]] wrote "the idea behind stamped money is sound",<ref name="Keynes"/> but he also contended that Gesell's proposed demurrage fees could be evaded by the use of more liquid competing forms of money and that inflation was therefore a preferable method to achieve economic stimulation.<ref name="Keynes"/>
However, Scottish economist [[Ahmed Anwar]] argues that Keynes' objection to demurrage currency is flawed and contrary to Gresham's law.<ref name="anwar-2020">{{cite journal |last=Anwar |first=Ahmed |date=December 2020 |title=From Keynes' Liquidity Preference to Gesell's Basic Interest |url=https://www.ed.ac.uk/files/atoms/files/from_keynes_liquidity_preference_to_gesells_basic_interest.pdf |journal=Discussion Paper Series |volume=299 |publisher=University of Edinburgh School of Economics |pages=29 |access-date=26 May 2025 |archive-date=7 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207104253/https://www.ed.ac.uk/files/atoms/files/from_keynes_liquidity_preference_to_gesells_basic_interest.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>
Keynes has also been accused of contradicting himself within the same paragraph: if he truly believed that people would prefer more liquid forms of currency over stamped money, then stamped money would not be a sound idea as he had said.<ref name="sidman-lecture-6-keynes">{{cite AV media |last=Sidman |first=Josh |date=3 April 2024 |title="Silvio Gesell: Beyond Capitalism vs Socialism" Class #6 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1GjX4PCcTlU%3Ft%3D2091 |time=34:51 |type=Video |language=English |publisher=Henry George School of Economics |access-date=23 May 2025 |archive-date=15 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815181623/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1GjX4PCcTlU%3Ft%3D2091 |url-status=live }}</ref>

One of the main barriers to the success of any demurrage currency is establishing it as a trusted medium of exchange.
People generally only accept payments in a currency when they believe that it will be accepted in future exchanges.
When businesses do not accept a type of money, workers usually refuse to receive it as payment.<ref name="cleveland-fed-2008"/>
Additionally, [[Jérôme Blanc]] argues that past experiments on demurrage currency relied heavily on both a distrust in the value of conventional money, as well as trust among a local community.
Although past experiments have worked successfully in small towns, they may not be as effective across an entire country, unless there is a way to ensure that trust in demurrage currency can scale with the size of the population that uses it.<ref name="blanc-1998">{{cite journal |last=Blanc |first=Jérôme |date=October 1998 |title=Free Money for Social Progress: Theory and Practice of Gesell's Accelerated Money |url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/3487118 |journal=American Journal of Economics and Sociology |volume=57 |issue=4 |pages=469–483 |doi=10.1111/j.1536-7150.1998.tb03376.x |jstor=3487118 |access-date=25 May 2025 |archive-date=11 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231111052252/https://www.jstor.org/stable/3487118 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=gomez-2018/>{{rp|p=12}}

None of the localities that have used demurrage currency in the past and present have fully implemented all three of the main proposals of Gesell's Freiwirtschaft.
Since only the Freigeld aspect of the theory and proposal has been tested, the Freiland and Freihandel aspects of the theory would also need to be implemented simultaneously, in order to observe how a Freiwirtschaft economy would work as a whole.<ref name="sidman-lecture-8">{{cite AV media |last=Sidman |first=Josh |date=17 April 2024 |title="Silvio Gesell: Beyond Capitalism vs Socialism" Class #8 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KqJNMM-aDVw%3Ft%3D2498 |time=41:38 |type=Video |language=English |publisher=Henry George School of Economics |access-date=25 May 2025 |archive-date=5 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250605010445/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KqJNMM-aDVw%3Ft%3D2498 |url-status=live }}</ref>

According to economist {{ill|Dirk Löhr|de}}, while demurrage currency has successfully worked on local scales in the past and present, and while Freiland reform is possible without Freigeld reform, there is an economic consensus that successful large-scale Freigeld monetary reform will not be possible without Freiland reform.<ref name="sidman-lecture-7">{{cite AV media |last=Sidman |first=Josh |date=10 April 2024 |title="Silvio Gesell: Beyond Capitalism vs Socialism" Class #7 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jeClotFiTDA%3Ft%3D2122 |time=35:22 |type=Video |language=English |publisher=Henry George School of Economics |access-date=30 April 2025 |archive-date=5 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250605010441/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jeClotFiTDA%3Ft%3D2122 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="wise">{{cite book |last=Wise |first=Leonard |date=1949 |title=Great Money Reformers. No. 1: Silvio Gesell |location=London |publisher=Holborn Publishing and Distg. Company |isbn= |page=9 |quote=Unless the reform of money is accompanied by the reform of land tenure, the advantages of money reform will be cornered by the private land owners. Land, then being the only source of unearned income, its owners could demand any amount of rent, either in rentals or prices of products.}}</ref>
The reason is that if money can no longer be used as a long-term store of wealth, then most people would shift to storing their wealth within land instead, since landowners would still retain unjustified rents due to the scarcity of land.<ref name="ilgmann-2011">{{cite journal |last1=Ilgmann |first1=Cordelius |date=April 2011 |title=Silvio Gesell: 'a strange, unduly neglected' monetary theorist |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/48540611 |journal=Journal of Post Keynesian Economics |volume=38 |issue=4 |publisher=Routledge |pages=532–564 |doi=10.1080/01603477.2015.1099446 |jstor=48540611 |access-date=26 April 2026}}</ref><ref name="soliani-2013">{{cite journal |last1=Soliani |first1=Riccardo |date=16 November 2013 |title=Establishing a natural economic order through free-land and free money by Silvio Gesell |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/43574364 |journal=Journal of Economics |volume=111 |issue=3 |publisher=Springer-Verlag Wien |pages=301–304 |doi=10.1007/s00712-013-0380-2 |jstor=43574364 |access-date=26 April 2026 |quote=Free-Money goes with Free-Land because competition occurs equitably only if privileges over the land are abolished.}}</ref>
If land reform is unfeasible for any reason, then large-scale Freigeld reform will be unlikely to have its intended effects.<ref name="sidman-lecture-7"/>

Professors Nikolaus Läufer and Gerhard Rösl argued that demurrage currencies can only increase economic activity temporarily.<ref name="depre"/> They believe that although the velocity of money would increase in the short-term, the total amount in circulation would gradually decrease, since demurrage currencies lose value over time. The lengthy use of demurrage currencies would thus ultimately lead to a decline in economic activity and economic instability.<ref>{{cite web|last=Läufer|first=Nikolaus|title=Natural Economic Order Theories or Freiwirtschaftslehre (Silvio Gesell)|url=http://www.uni-konstanz.de/FuF/wiwi/laufer/main.html#FREI|publisher=University of Konstanz|access-date=3 April 2014|date=31 December 2006|language=de|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121120232834/http://www.uni-konstanz.de/FuF/wiwi/laufer/main.html#FREI|archive-date=20 November 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>{{clarify |date=June 2015 |reason=More specific link required}} However, Gesell supported allowing a [[monetary authority]] to monitor the money supply. If the amount of money in circulation falls too much, the monetary authority would print more money.<ref name="dillard-1997"/><ref name="baynham-2023"/> The sole mandate of the money issuing authority would be to maintain stable prices, so the money supply would not necessarily remain constant. If prices rise, then the money supply would be reduced, and vice versa.

Gesell believed that Freiwirtschaft would create Darwinian [[natural selection]] in the economy: "[[Free competition]] would favor the efficient and lead to their increased propagation."<ref name="baynham-2023"/> [[Marxist]]s such as the academic [[Elmar Altvater]] described Freigeld as a "[[Social Darwinist]] concept" and criticized its past supporters for trying to ally with the [[Nazi Party]], even though the Nazis ignored their ideas.<ref name="altvater">{{cite web |url=http://userpage.fu-berlin.de/~roehrigw/altvater/altvater.pdf |title=Eine andere Welt mit welchem Geld? |trans-title=Another world with what money? |last=Altvater |first=Elmar |website=Freie Universität Berlin |access-date=27 April 2025 |archive-date=18 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250818155649/http://userpage.fu-berlin.de/~roehrigw/altvater/altvater.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> {{ill|Werner Onken|de}} replied to this accusation that the [[theory of evolution]] was new at that time and existed in contrast to the dogmas of [[Christianity]] above all. Onken wrote that Gesell did not represent a "struggle of the strongest against the weaker", as he instead advocated "to create the conditions for a just distribution of income and wealth".<ref name="onken-on-darwinism">{{cite web |url=http://userpage.fu-berlin.de/~roehrigw/onken/attac2004/dresden-onken.htm#_ftnref31 |title=Für eine andere Welt mit einem anderen Geld – Sind die Geldreformer wirklich Antisemiten? |trans-title=For another world with another money: Are the money reformers really anti-Semites? |last=Onken |first=Werner |date=31 December 2004 |website=Freie Universität Berlin |access-date=27 April 2025 |archive-date=22 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250222180226/https://userpage.fu-berlin.de/~roehrigw/onken/attac2004/dresden-onken.htm#_ftnref31 |url-status=live }}</ref>
Gesell also believed that the extremes of wealth inequality signified structural defects in the economy, and were thus undeserved.<ref name="onken-2000"/>

== History ==
=== Pre-modern usage ===
Bernard Lietaer documents in his book ''Mysterium Geld'' the use of demurrage currency systems in [[Europe]]'s [[High Middle Ages]]' [[bracteate]] systems and [[ancient Egypt]]'s [[ostracon|ostraka]] – dated receipts for the storage of grain – and credits these currency systems with the prosperity of those societies.<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|pp=5–6}}<ref name="svensson"/> One notable example of demurrage is the founder of the [[Mark of Brandenburg]], [[Albert the Bear]].<ref name="lietaer-2000">{{cite book |last=Lietaer |first=Bernard A. |date=2000 |title=Mysterium Geld. Emotionale Bedeutung und Wirkungsweise eines Tabus. |trans-title=Mystery of Money |publisher=Riemann Verlag |isbn=978-3570500095}}</ref>

The [[Islam]]ic system of [[zakat]] sometimes works as a form of demurrage tax, but not always since it applies to assets generally, not currency specifically.
Zakat on wealth is based on the value of all of one's possessions.<ref>Décobert, C. (1991), ''Le mendiant et le combattant, L’institution de l’islam'', Paris: Éditions du Seuil, pp. 238–240.</ref><ref>Medani Ahmed and Sebastian Gianci, ''Zakat'', Encyclopedia of Taxation and Tax Policy, p. 479, quote: "As one of the Islam's five pillars, zakat becomes an obligation due when, over a lunar year, one controls a combination of income and wealth equal to or above [[Nisaab]]."</ref> It is customarily 2.5% (or {{frac|40}})<ref>{{cite book|last1=Sarwar|first1=Muhammad|title=al-Kafi Volume 1 of 8|date=2015|publisher=The Islamic Seminary Inc.|location=New York|isbn=978-0-9914308-6-4|page=345|edition=2nd|ref=H 918}}</ref> of a Muslim's total savings and wealth above a minimum amount known as ''[[nisab]]'' each lunar year,<ref name=yaqaradawi>Yusuf al-Qaradawi (1999), Monzer Kahf (transl.), Fiqh az-Zakat, Dar al Taqwa, London, Volume 1, {{ISBN|978-967-5062-766}}, p. xix.</ref> but Islamic scholars differ on how much ''nisab'' is and other aspects of zakat.<ref name=yaqaradawi/>
Today, in most [[Muslim-majority countries]], zakat contributions are voluntary, while in [[Libya]], [[Malaysia]], [[Pakistan]], [[Saudi Arabia]], [[Sudan]] and [[Yemen]], zakat is mandated and collected by the state (as of 2015).<ref name="Marty-1996-p.320">{{cite book|author1=Marty, Martin E. |author2=Appleby, R. Scott |name-list-style=amp |title=Fundamentalisms and the state: remaking polities, economies, and militance|publisher=University of Chicago Press|year=1996|isbn=978-0-226-50884-9|page=320|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=doCmVaOnh_wC&pg=PA320}}</ref><ref name=Hasan>{{cite book|author=Samiul Hasan|title=Human Security and Philanthropy: Islamic Perspectives and Muslim Majority Country Practices|publisher=Springer|year=2015|page=130|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-JVwCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA130|isbn=978-1493925254}}</ref>

=== Guernsey experiment of 1815 ===
In 1815, there was a money experiment on [[Guernsey]] in the British [[Channel Islands]].
The consequences of the [[Napoleonic Wars]] were noticeable throughout Europe, including on this island.
The islanders produced food far beyond its own needs, but the collected taxes and interest payments to London banks finally brought payments to a halt.
The incumbent governor of Guernsey, Daniel de Lisle Brock, proposed the construction of a market hall for 4000 pounds sterling to give the economy a new impetus.
These 4000 pounds were printed and put into circulation as a [[complementary currency]].
After five years, the hall had fully amortized, which means that it had fully earned its depreciation and the 4000 pounds, which had now been in circulation on the whole of the island and had caused all kinds of revenues, were again available to the investor of the market hall, and were no longer needed and burned.

According to this principle, several building projects with self-printed and later again destroyed building projects were realized one after the other.
However, by 1835, the intervention of foreign banks and a reduced money supply caused the economy to come to a standstill again.
Some supporters of Freiwirtschaft, including {{ill|Hermann Benjes|de}}, regard the "Miracle of Guernsey" as a precursor to demurrage money,<ref>{{cite book |last=Benjes |first=Hermann |title=Das Mirakel von Guernsey |trans-title=The Miracles of Guernsey |date=2003 |publisher=H. Benjes |edition=sixth |isbn=3-00-000204-9 |url=https://www.sffo.de/sffo/Guernsey_freigeld.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208154437/http://www.sffo.de/sffo/Guernsey_freigeld.pdf |archive-date=8 December 2015 |access-date=11 May 2025}}</ref> after Silvio Gesell, who wrote an article about the experiment.<ref>{{cite book |last=Gesell |first=Silvio |date=1922 |title=Die Guernsey-Markthalle. In: Die Freiwirtschaft durch Freiland und Freigeld |trans-title=The Guernsey Market Hall. The free economy through free land and free money |series=Silvio Gesell: Gesammelte Werke, Gauke Verlag für Sozialökonomie |location= <!-- omit without publisher: Kiel, Germany --> |volume=14}}</ref>
The [[Guernsey pound]] is still used today.<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|p=7}}

=== 1890s and early 1900s ===
{{Main|Silvio Gesell#Life}}
The application of deliberate demurrage rates on currency was first theorized to have economic benefits by Silvio Gesell in the 1890s.
Gesell first started thinking about the structural problems caused by the [[money|monetary system]] after the [[Baring crisis|1890 depression in Argentina]] hurt his business considerably.<ref name="Keynes"/>
Gesell released his first theoretical writing on currency: "The Reformation of the Monetary System as a Bridge to a Social State"<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Blanc |first1=Jérôme |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/5088112|title=Silvio Gesell's Theory and Accelerated Money Experiments |date=February 1998 }}</ref> ({{langx|de|Die Reformation des Münzwesens als Brücke zum sozialen Staat}}, 1891).
He also wrote and published ''The Nerve of Things'' ({{langx|la|Nervus rerum}}, 1891) and "The nationalization of money"<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://theanarchistlibrary.org/library/silvio-gesell-the-natural-economic-order|title=The Natural Economic Order|via=theanarchistlibrary.org|archive-date=17 March 2025|access-date=30 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250317140424/https://theanarchistlibrary.org/library/silvio-gesell-the-natural-economic-order|url-status=live}}</ref> ({{langx|de|Die Verstaatlichung des Geldes, 1892}}).<ref name="Keynes"/>
In 1916, Gesell later published his most famous work on demurrage, ''The Natural Economic Order''.

After Gesell died in 1930, many localities were inspired by his economic theories and tried using demurrage currencies to alleviate their local economies during the [[Great Depression]].

=== Great Depression ===
==== Europe ====
Schwanenkirchen, [[Bavaria]] was among the first towns ever to test Gesell's Freiwirtschaft proposals.
In 1929, the owner of a bankrupt coal mine, Max Hebecker, decided to pay two-thirds of his workers' salaries in a currency known as the [[Wära]], which was [[fixed exchange rate|pegged]] to the [[Reichsmark]].
By 1931, the coal mine was restarted, the Wära was widely used in Schwanenkirchen and the local economy greatly improved, and the currency was used by over 2000 businesses from all over Germany.
In November 1931, the German Central Bank outlawed the currency, and economic stagnation continued.<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|p=6}}

[[File:Freigeld1.jpg|thumb|One Schilling note with demurrage stamps from [[Wörgl]]]]
Demurrage-charged [[local currency]] was tested in the Austrian town of [[Wörgl]] between 1932 and 1934, as a tax collected for the benefit of the unemployed.
Due to the local currency's success in reducing unemployment and increasing economic activity, at least 200 cities across Austria formed plans to mimic the currency system in Wörgl.<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|p=7}}
However, these plans were never realized since Austria's central bank [[Oesterreichische Nationalbank]] outlawed complementary currencies in the country on 1 September 1933, so that the federal government would maintain a monopoly on the country's currency and legal tender.<ref name="Boyle 2002">{{Cite book|last=Boyle|first=David|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=glqnzC-TLPMC&dq=worgl+miracle&pg=RA1-PA237|title=The Money Changers: Currency Reform from Aristotle to E-cash|date=2002|publisher=Earthscan|isbn=978-1-85383-895-8}}</ref><ref name="Cornell University Press">{{Cite book|last1=Helleiner|first1=Eric|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gJX1buNKHj0C&dq=worgl+miracle&pg=PA159|title=The Making of National Money: Territorial Currencies in Historical Perspective|last2=Helleiner|first2=Faculty of Arts Chair in International Political Economy Professor Eric|date=2003|publisher=Cornell University Press|isbn=978-0-8014-4049-6}}</ref>

In 1933, a National Committee of the Mutual Exchanges was formed in [[Nice]], France, which created trade vouchers intended to circulate only between members, mainly traders. (The Committee's statutes appeared in the press on 12 September, the creation of the association being officially announced at the Olympic Day on 10 December of the same year). Under the ministry of Laval, the Banque de France intervened and declared the experiment illegal. After World War II, a jeweler by the name of Soriano, who participated in this experiment, gave his support for "the libre commune of Lignières-en-Berry".
<ref name="Deffeyes 1995">Catherine Célimène et Guy Deffeyes, 1995, ''Le Nouveau Pari monnaie-terre; voyage au pays de l'art de dissoudre le chômage et quelques autres préjugés…'', janvier 1995, éditions Terre Active</ref><ref>Laacher Smaïn. L'État et les systèmes d'échanges locaux (SEL). Tensions et intentions à propos des notions de solidarité et d'intérêt général. In: Politix, vol. 11, n°42, Deuxième trimestre 1998. Définir l'intérêt général, sous la direction de Brigitte Gaïti, Arthur Jobert et Jérôme Valluy. pp. 123–149</ref>

In August 1936, the city of [[Montoro]] issued what might have been the first demurrage currency in all of Spain. The local council printed a series of five-[[Spanish peseta|peseta]] bills, each with a depreciation table on one side.
The value of bills decreased weekly. For example, a bill that was worth five pesetas on November 1 would be worth 4.50 pesetas on November 8.
If the bills remained unused after twelve weeks, they would be only partially redeemable at the town hall. There were similar monetary experiments in [[Porcuna]] and other locations in Spain that were ruled by the [[Popular Front (Spain)|Popular Front]] in [[Province of Córdoba (Spain)|Córdoba province]] in 1936–1937.<ref name=gomez-2018/>{{rp|p=15}}

At the end of the [[Spanish Civil War]], [[Francisco Franco]]'s government confiscated and voided all [[Second Spanish Republic|Republican]] money, municipal coins, and local banknotes. Meanwhile, Franco decreed that all the municipal currencies issued by the [[Nationalist faction (Spanish Civil War)|winning national army]] could be exchanged at the [[Bank of Spain]] for the new Spanish currency (Order 5, Decree 27 August 1938 published on 17 September 1938).
Despite being prohibited, many complementary currencies continued to circulate among the population as a medium of exchange for years after the Spanish Civil War (1939–1955).<ref name=gomez-2018/>{{rp|p=15}}

The [[WIR Bank]] was founded in 1934 by Swiss businessmen Werner Zimmermann and Paul Enz as a result of currency shortages and global financial instability.<ref name="tobias-1998"/>
Both Zimmermann and Enz had been influenced by Gesell's monetary theory.
The bank circulated demurrage currency from 1936 to 1948, until it renounced Gesell's theory.<ref name="tobias-1998"/>
The WIR Bank was a not-for-profit entity, although that status changed during the Bank's expansion.<ref name="WIR-2010">{{cite web | title=Press Release 2010 Annual report of the WIR Bank | work=WIR Bank | url=http://www.wir.ch/index.cfm?uuid=CBD9201A3DBB11D6B9950001020761E5&and_uuid=A418FC335056B8078ABF3FC01C5D51CE | accessdate=22 March 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120325013519/http://www.wir.ch/index.cfm?uuid=CBD9201A3DBB11D6B9950001020761E5&and_uuid=A418FC335056B8078ABF3FC01C5D51CE | archive-date=25 March 2012 | url-status=dead | df=dmy-all }}</ref>

==== North America ====
{{See also|Ham and Eggs movement}}
Local stamp scrip systems, many of which incorporated demurrage fees, were used in at least 450 cities during the [[Great Depression in the United States]].<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|p=7}}
Most scrip was issued in late 1932 and early 1933 before [[Franklin Roosevelt]] succeeded the presidency, and when bank suspensions were the most frequent and widespread.
The New Jersey, Ohio, Michigan, Indiana, North Dakota, Tennessee, and North Carolina state legislatures all passed laws allowing localities in their respective states to issue stamp scrip.<ref name="cleveland-fed-2008"/><ref name="wolfgang-2007">Wolfgang Broer: ''Schwundgeld: Bürgermeister Michael Unterguggenberger und das Wörgler Währungsexperiment 1932/33'', 2007, p. 323, {{ISBN|3706544725}}, 9783706544726.</ref>
Iowa even went as far as to propose issuing statewide stamp scrip, but never enacted it.<ref name="iowa-stamp-scrip">{{cite web |url=https://pubs.lib.uiowa.edu/annals-of-iowa/article/5933/galley/114735/view/ |title=Iowa Stamp Scrip: Economic Experimentation in Iowa Communities during the Great Depression |last=Warner |first=Jonathan |date=2012 |website=University of Iowa |publisher=The State Historical Society of Iowa |access-date=21 April 2025 |archive-date=7 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251207183920/https://pubs.lib.uiowa.edu/annals-of-iowa/article/5933/galley/114735/view/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
Oregon planned to print $80 million of stamp scrip in 1933, but was stopped by the U.S. Treasury.<ref name="baynham-2023"/>
The experiments became so popular that the economist [[Irving Fisher]] decided to analyze them.
Fisher criticized how most of the scrip that was used in the US was undated, since dated scrip would have been necessary to incentivize users to buy stamps for renewing the value of the scrip.<ref name="cleveland-fed-2008"/>
Fisher instead recommended issuing dated stamp scrip nationwide in his book ''Stamp Scrip'', but President Roosevelt rejected Fisher's recommendations.<ref name="fisher-stamp-scrip">{{cite book |last=Fisher |first=Irving |year=1933 |title=Stamp Scrip |url=https://userpage.fu-berlin.de/roehrigw/fisher/ |location=New York |access-date=18 April 2025 |archive-date=23 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250323145737/https://userpage.fu-berlin.de/roehrigw/fisher/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="depre">{{cite news|title=Depreciating currencies: The money-go-round|url=https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2009/01/22/the-money-go-round|access-date=8 February 2018|newspaper=The Economist|date=22 January 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20230209224329/https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2009/01/22/the-money-go-round|archive-date=9 February 2023}}</ref>

Fisher composed the Bankhead-Pettengill bill that was introduced to Congress by Senator [[John H. Bankhead II]] of Alabama on February 17, 1933.
Fisher proposed a nationwide issue of up to $1 billion in $1 dated stamp scrip as legal tender under the US Treasury, but the bill never came to a vote.
Similar bills were subsequently proposed in Congress, but none succeeded.<ref name="cleveland-fed-2008"/>
In March 1933, President Franklin Roosevelt issued an executive order that banned all further issues of stamp scrip out of fear that the federal government would lose its authority over the monetary system.<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|p=7}}<ref name=gomez-2018/>{{rp|p=12}}<ref name="monbiot-2009">{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2009/jan/20/george-monbiot-recession-currencies |title=If the state can't save us, we need a licence to print our own money |last=Monbiot |first=George |date=19 January 2009 |website=The Guardian |publisher=Guardian News & Media Limited |access-date=2 November 2025 |quote=Roosevelt prohibited complementary currencies by executive decree, though they might have offered a faster, cheaper and more effective means of pulling the US out of the Depression than his New Deal.}}</ref> which arguably prolonged the [[Great Depression]].<ref name="monbiot-2009"/>

In 1936, the [[Social Credit Party of Canada|Social Credit Party]]-led government in Alberta, Canada, introduced [[prosperity certificates]] in an attempt to alleviate the effects of the Great Depression, with holders having to affix to the back of a certificate a 1-cent stamp before the end of every week, for the certificate to maintain its validity.

=== Post-World War II ===
The major [[central bank]]s' post-World War II policy of steady [[monetary inflation]] as proposed by Keynes was influenced by Gesell's idea of demurrage currency,<ref name="Keynes"/> but used inflation of the money supply rather than fees to increase the velocity of money in an attempt to expand the economy.

On 9 September 1950, the Free Social Party was founded in Germany with a platform based on Gesell's Freiwirtschaft theory. After a few name changes, it has been known as the {{ill|Human Economics Party|de|Humanwirtschaftspartei|es|Partido Economía Humana}} ({{langx|de|Humanwirtschaftspartei}}) since 28 April 2001.<ref>{{cite web |title=Grundsatzprogramm der Humanwirtschaftspartei |trans-title=Basic program of the Human Economy Party |url=http://humanwirtschaftspartei.de/partei/partei-grundsatzprogramm/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208104459/http://humanwirtschaftspartei.de/partei/partei-grundsatzprogramm/ |archive-date=8 December 2015}}</ref>

Two brief experiments took place in [[Cher (department)|Cher]], France in 1956 and [[Charente-Maritime]], France in 1957 respectively. Issued by an association under the term "vouchers" or "work vouchers", these demurrage currencies were abandoned in December 1958 following the adoption of an ordinance prohibiting "the issuance or putting into circulation of means of payment intended to replace or replace legal tender signs".<ref>Ferreira, Nathalie. « De la réforme du système monétaire à la monnaie sociale : l’apport théorique de P.J. Proudhon (1809–1865). » L'Actualité économique, volume 86, numéro 2, juin 2010, p. 205–225.</ref>

Pierre Tournadre, a watchmaker, and Georges Lardeau, director of a cinema, who faced rural exodus and economic decline, declared on 26 April 1956 "the libre commune of Lignières-en-Berry". The demurrage money was issued in August 1956. As word of the experiment spread, the government started tabling a bill in December to try to ban the currencies. In June 1957, a judicial police investigation pressed no charges. The journal ''Science et Vie'' (Étienne Dugue, La monnaie accelerated, number 488, May 1958) noted that this experiment ended on 24 December 1958, due to the passage of ordinance 58-1298.<ref>{{cite web |last=Guillemain |first=Gilles |url=https://www.lanouvellerepublique.fr/actu/la-lignieres-pour-dynamiser-l-economie-locale |title=La lignières pour dynamiser l'économie locale |date=10 February 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241130190647/https://www.lanouvellerepublique.fr/indre/la-lignieres-pour-dynamiser-l-economie-locale |archive-date=30 November 2024 |access-date=18 July 2026}}</ref><ref name="Deffeyes 1995" />

=== Great Recession ===
The [[Great Recession]] inspired many communities to establish local demurrage currencies.
There are currently a handful of demurrage currencies that are still used today.<ref name="cato-2012"/>

In [[Shaymuratovo]], Bashkortostan, Russia, the town's declining agricultural enterprise implemented a demurrage currency in 2010, in the wake of the Great Recession. The government believed that this was a violation of labor laws and shut the currency down. The community tried to implement a demurrage currency once more, but this time as [[gift card]]s, instead of an official currency. People were paid their full salaries in rubles, but could then buy the new currency in the company stores and buy goods with the new currency. Overall, the experiment caused commodity turnover to increase dramatically. Productivity increased, [[arrear]]s were paid off, and salaries increased. The surrounding region took notice and other businesses started to accept the currency, whether from the experiment or from the improving business climate in general. Although the goal of saving the business was achieved and the economy was stabilized, the government once again tried to stop the experiment multiple times, leading to its retirement after a few years.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://blog.hasslberger.com/2013/02/bashkir_farmers_local_demurrag.html |title=Bashkir farmers' local demurrage currency recognized by Supreme Court |last=Hasslberger |first=Sepp |date=5 February 2013 |website=Sepp Hasslberger |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250605010416/http://blog.hasslberger.com/2013/02/bashkir_farmers_local_demurrag.html |archive-date=5 June 2025 |access-date=2 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="shaymuratovo-2025">{{cite web |url=https://laweba.net/dengi-shaymuratiki-v-shaymuratovo |title=Money: Shaimurots in Shaimuratovo |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250605091722/https://laweba.net/dengi-shaymuratiki-v-shaymuratovo |archive-date=5 June 2025}}</ref>

== List ==
=== Current currencies ===
[[File:Chiemgauer-Fächer.jpg|thumb|[[Chiemgauer]] notes (2008 issue). Between 2003 and 2015, a "scrip" corresponding to 2% of the banknote value had to be paid every three months and affixed to the front of the bill in order to maintain an individual bill's validity.<ref name="gelleri-2009">{{cite journal|last1=Gelleri|first1=Christian|title=Chiemgauer Regiomoney: Theory and Practice of a Currency |journal=International Journal of Community Currency Research|date=2009|volume=13|pages=61–75|url= https://ijccr.files.wordpress.com/2012/05/ijccrvol132009pp61-75gelleri.pdf }}</ref>]]
* [[Chiemgauer]], a community currency in [[Bavaria]], Germany, started in 2003. As of 2021, the demurrage rate is 6% per year, or 3% every six months for paper money.<ref name="gelleri-2021">{{cite journal |last1=Gelleri |first1=Christian |last2=Stodder |first2=James |date=2021 |title=Chiemgauer complementary currency – concept, effects, and econometric analysis |url=https://ijccr.net/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/75_95-ijccr_2021_1-gelleri.pdf |journal=International Journal of Community Currency Research |volume=25 |issue=1 |pages=75–95 |doi=10.15133/j.ijccr.2021.006 |access-date=7 August 2025 |archive-date=15 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815093724/https://ijccr.net/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/75_95-ijccr_2021_1-gelleri.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> In the [[Digital currency|digital form]] of the Chiemgauer, the demurrage rate is calculated daily (6% divided by 365 days = 0.016% per day).<ref name="gelleri-2021"/> The demurrage rate does not start until after holding the currency for the first 90 days.<ref name="gelleri-2021"/> Between 2003 and 2015, the demurrage rate was 2% per quarter, or 8% per year.<ref name="gelleri-2009"/>
* Peanuts, a local currency that was created in [[Chiba Prefecture]], Japan in February 1999 as a part of the Eco-Money Network.<ref name="sahakian-2017">{{cite journal |last=Sahakian |first=Marlyne |date=5 October 2017 |title=Complementary currencies: what opportunities for sustainable consumption in times of crisis and beyond? |journal=Sustainability: Science, Practice and Policy |volume=10 |issue=1 |publisher=Taylor & Francis Online |pages=10–11 |doi=10.1080/15487733.2014.11908121 |issn=1548-7733 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Peanuts has a demurrage charge of 1% per month, and is used by over 600 participants, including local businesses, farmers, and individuals.<ref name="lietaer-japan">{{cite journal |last1=Lietaer |first1=Bernard |date=May 2003 |title=Complementary Currencies in Japan Today: History, Originality, and Relevance |journal=International Journal of Community Currency Research |volume=8 |url=https://ijccr.net/wp-content/uploads/2012/05/ijccr-vol-8-2004-1-lietaer.pdf |publisher=IJCCR.net |pages=14 |access-date=23 May 2025 |archive-date=23 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251123130145/https://ijccr.net/wp-content/uploads/2012/05/ijccr-vol-8-2004-1-lietaer.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Freicoin, a [[crypto-currency]] that was developed by Mark Friedenbach and launched on 17 December 2012. Freicoin has a demurrage rate of ~4.9% per year, which discourages price [[speculation]] and theoretically makes Freicoin a superior medium of exchange, compared to [[Bitcoin]].<ref name="steadman-2013">{{cite web |url=http://arstechnica.com/business/2013/05/wary-of-bitcoin-a-guide-to-some-other-cryptocurrencies/2/ |title= Wary of Bitcoin? A guide to some other cryptocurrencies |last=Steadman |first=Ian |date=11 May 2013 |website=Ars Technica |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130514022405/http://arstechnica.com/business/2013/05/wary-of-bitcoin-a-guide-to-some-other-cryptocurrencies/2/ |archive-date=14 May 2013 |access-date=26 May 2025}}</ref>
* [[Abeille (local currency)|Abeille]], a community currency in [[Villeneuve-sur-Lot]], France, started in 2010. To maintain an individual bill's validity, a stamp scrip corresponding to 2% of the banknote value must be paid every six months.<ref name="ladepeche-2010">{{cite web |url=https://www.ladepeche.fr/article/2010/01/20/758943-villeneuve-les-abeilles-arrivent-dans-les-porte-monnaie.html |title=Villeneuve. Les abeilles arrivent dans les porte-monnaie |trans-title=Villeneuve. Bees arrive in the wallets |date=20 January 2010 |website=La Dépêche du Midi |access-date=26 May 2025 |archive-date=29 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029004458/http://www.ladepeche.fr/article/2010/01/20/758943-villeneuve-les-abeilles-arrivent-dans-les-porte-monnaie.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
* [[Occitan (local currency)|Occitan]], a community currency in [[Languedoc-Roussillon]], France, started in 2010. It is interest-free and designed to circulate faster.<ref name="herault-2009">{{cite web |url=https://www.herault-tribune.com/articles/pezenas-une-nouvelle-monnaie-locale-loccitan/ |last=ACAI Office |title=Pézenas: Une nouvelle monnaie locale, l'Occitan |trans-title=Pézenas: A new local currency, the Occitan |date=29 November 2009 |website=Herault Tribune |access-date=26 May 2025 |archive-date=19 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250519172352/https://www.herault-tribune.com/articles/pezenas-une-nouvelle-monnaie-locale-loccitan/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Defunct currencies ===
* In [[ancient Egypt]], [[ostracon|ostraka]] – dated receipts for the storage of grain – functioned as a demurrage currency.<ref name="lietaer-2000"/> Ostraka was used in Egypt until the end of the [[Ptolemaic Kingdom]], after which it was forcefully replaced by Roman currency.<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|pp=5–6}}
* ''[[Bracteate#High medieval bracteates|Renovatio Monetae]]'' was a monetary system during the [[High Middle Ages]] where coins had to be called back and exchanged for new coins regularly, about once or twice a year.<ref name="lietaer-2000"/><ref name="svensson"/>
* [[Wära]], a local currency used in Schwanenkirchen, [[Bavaria]] and later other German cities as one of the first [[Freiwirtschaft|free economy]] experiments. It was introduced by [[Hans Timm]] and [[Helmut Rödiger]], who were followers of [[Silvio Gesell]]. It was introduced in 1926, and operated until it was shut down by the German Central Bank and the Reich Ministry of Finance.<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|p=6}}
* {{ill|Wörgler Schwundgeld|de}}, the currency of the [[Wörgl#The Wörgl Experiment|Wörgl Experiment]]. Began on 31 July 1932 and ended by Austria's central bank [[Oesterreichische Nationalbank]] on 1 September 1933.<ref name="Boyle 2002"/><ref name="Cornell University Press"/>
* Local currency "stamp scrip" experiments were conducted in several cities in the United States during the 1930s.<ref name="iowa-stamp-scrip"/><ref name="wolfgang-2007"/><ref name="cleveland-fed-2008"/> In March 1933, President Franklin Roosevelt banned all further issues of stamp scrip out of fear that the federal government would lose its authority over the monetary system,<ref name="lietaer-1990"/>{{rp|p=7}}<ref name=gomez-2018/>{{rp|p=12}}<ref name="monbiot-2009"/> which arguably prolonged the [[Great Depression]].<ref name="monbiot-2009"/>
* [[Prosperity certificate]], a local currency in [[Alberta]], Canada that existed in 1936.<ref>Charlton Standard Catalogue of Canadian Government Paper Money, {{ISSN|1716-0731}}, 18th edition, p. 13.  Charlton Press.</ref>
* [[WIR Bank]], a bank founded by Swiss businessmen Werner Zimmermann and Paul Enz that circulated demurrage currency from 1936 to 1948.<ref name="tobias-1998">{{cite book |first=Tobias |last=Studer |year=1998 |title=WIR and the Swiss National Economy |publisher=WIR Bank, Basel |pages=59}}</ref>
* [[Crédito]], an Argentine interest-free<ref name="DeMeulenaere-2000">{{cite web| title=Reinventing the Market: Alternative Currencies and Community Development in Argentina| work=International Journal of Community Currency Research 2000, Volume 4| url=http://www.le.ac.uk/ulmc/ijccr/vol4-6/4no3.htm| accessdate=July 30, 2005| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050321092701/http://www.le.ac.uk/ulmc/ijccr/vol4-6/4no3.htm| archive-date=March 21, 2005| url-status=dead |issn=1325-9547}}</ref> community currency, started on 1 May 1995 that lost most of its popularity in the early 2000s. Some variants of the Crédito that were used in the Argentinian barter clubs of the late 1990s and the early 2000s allegedly used demurrage.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} At its peak, the Crédito was used by a few million people.<ref name="sahakian-2017"/>
* [[E-gold]], a [[private currency|private]] [[digital gold currency]] where there was a gold storage charge of 1% per annum. The demurrage associated with e-gold is arguably expended by the currency operator to help cover real storage costs.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}} E-gold was launched in 1996, and suspended in 2009 due to legal issues.
* [[Stroud pound]], a community currency in [[Stroud]], [[Gloucestershire]], England, started in 2009. The Stroud pound was inspired by the Chiemgauer, and has a demurrage rate of 3% every six months.<ref name="cato-2012">{{cite journal |title=Stroud Pound: a Local Currency to Map, Measure and Strengthen The Local Economy |last1=Scott Cato |first1=Molly |author-link1=Molly Scott Cato |last2=Suárez |first2=Marta |journal=International Journal of Community Currency Research |date=July 2012 |volume=16 |pages=Section D 106–115 |url=https://ijccr.files.wordpress.com/2012/07/ijccr-2012-scott-cato-suarez.pdf |archive-date=15 October 2023 |access-date=27 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231015115603/https://ijccr.files.wordpress.com/2012/07/ijccr-2012-scott-cato-suarez.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> The website was last updated in 2012, and it no longer exists as of 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.stroudpound.org.uk/ |title=Home |website=stroudpound.org.uk |access-date=12 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150405112423/http://www.stroudpound.org.uk/ |archive-date=5 April 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> As of 2025, Stroud Pound Co-op Ltd still exists,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/06916671|title=STROUD POUND CO-OP LTD overview - Find and update company information - GOV.UK|website=find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk|access-date=20 October 2025|archive-date=23 December 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251223194615/https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/06916671|url-status=live}}</ref> but the Stroud pound is otherwise inactive.<ref name="sheffield-2017">{{cite web |url=https://thelongandshort.org/growth/new-money-do-local-currencies-actually-work |title=New money: Do local currencies actually work? |last=Sheffield |first=Hazel |date=13 January 2017 |website=The long and short |publisher=Nesta |access-date=7 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241117230847/https://thelongandshort.org/growth/new-money-do-local-currencies-actually-work |archive-date=17 November 2024}}</ref>
* Shenzhen [[DCEP]] in 2020: 50,000 lottery winners in Shenzhen's Luohu district were given 200 digital yuan each on 12 October 2020 and the money was programmed to expire on 18 October 2020. The goal was to boost consumer spending and test the currency and technology as a [[case study]].<ref name="cambridge-2025">{{cite journal |url=https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/~fms27/papers/2025-StajanoSamZi-expiring--weis.pdf |title=On the nature and security of expiring digital cash |last1=Stajano |first1=Frank |last2=Samaria |first2=Ferdinando |last3=Zi |first3=Shuqi |date=19 May 2025 |publisher=University of Cambridge |journal=Journal of Risk and Financial Management |doi=10.3390/jrfm18080452 |volume=18 |issue=8 |page=452 |doi-access=free |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260122140536/https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/~fms27/papers/2025-StajanoSamZi-expiring--weis.pdf |archive-date=22 January 2026 |url-status=live |access-date=19 July 2026}}</ref><ref name="ETBFSI-2021">{{cite web |url=https://bfsi.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/policy/digital-currency-yuan-comes-with-an-expiry-date-spend-or-it-will-vanish/82059471 |title=Digital Currency: Yuan comes with an expiry date: Spend or it will vanish |last=Banking financial services and insurance |first=Economic Times |date=14 April 2021 |website=India Times |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260526161306/https://bfsi.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/policy/digital-currency-yuan-comes-with-an-expiry-date-spend-or-it-will-vanish/82059471 |archive-date=26 May 2026 |url-status=live |access-date=19 July 2026}}</ref><ref name="bossone-2022">{{cite web |url=https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/allaboutfinance/expiring-money-part-i |title=Expiring money (Part I) |last1=Bossone |first1=Biagio |last2=Faragallah |first2=Ahmed |date=2 November 2022 |website=World Bank |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260309205633/https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/allaboutfinance/expiring-money-part-i |archive-date=9 March 2026 |url-status=live |access-date=19 July 2026}}</ref>

=== Proposed currencies ===
* A carry tax on currency was proposed by a [[Federal Reserve]] employee (Marvin Goodfriend) in 1999, to be implemented via magnetic strips on bills, deducting the carry tax upon deposit, the tax being based on how long the bill had been held.<ref name="wired-carry-tax">{{Cite magazine |last=McCullagh |first=Declan |date=27 October 1999 |title=Cash and the 'Carry Tax' |url=https://www.wired.com/1999/10/cash-and-the-carry-tax/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241215190252/https://www.wired.com/1999/10/cash-and-the-carry-tax/ |archive-date=2024-12-15 |access-date=2011-12-21 |magazine=WIRED}}</ref>
* [[Bernard Lietaer]]'s [[terra (proposed currency)|terra]] is a commodity basket currency proposal similar to Keynes's [[bancor]] or L'Europa (The idea to establish a L'Europa – monnaie de la paix from early concepts presented in an article in the French newspaper Le Fédériste on 1 January 1933) and bearing a demurrage charge.<ref name="lietaer-kiuchi-2004">{{Cite web |last=Lietaer |first=Bernard |author-link=Bernard Lietaer |editor-first=Takashi |editor-last=Kiuchi |title=The Terra TRC™ White Paper |date=2004 |url=https://bernard-lietaer.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/2004-The-Terra-TRC-White-Paper-Lietaer-annotated.pdf |access-date=27 May 2025 |archive-date=25 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251125064752/https://bernard-lietaer.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/2004-The-Terra-TRC-White-Paper-Lietaer-annotated.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="lietaer-future">{{Cite book |last=Lietaer |first=Bernard A. |author-link=Bernard Lietaer |title=The Future of Money: A new way to create wealth, work, and a wiser world |year=2001 |publisher=Century |location=London |isbn=0-7126-9991-0}}</ref>

=== Fictional currencies ===
* [[Michael Ende]] stated that he had the concept of demurrage currency in mind when writing his children's fantasy novel ''[[Momo (novel)|Momo]]''.<ref name="equilibrismus">[http://www.equilibrismus.de/en/topics/general/rm-michael_ende.htm Michael Ende's last words to the Japanese] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061010110240/http://www.equilibrismus.de/en/topics/general/rm-michael_ende.htm|date=2006-10-10}}.</ref> ''Momo'' features a currency that revolves around time, which can be exchanged between people.
* A negative interest rate could be levied on existing paper currency in principle via a [[serial number]] lottery, such as randomly choosing a number 0 through 9 and declaring that notes whose serial number end in that digit are worthless, yielding an average 10% loss of paper cash holdings to hoarders; a drawn two-digit number could match the last two digits on the note for a 1% loss. This was proposed by an anonymous student of [[Greg Mankiw]],<ref name="Gesell-NYT">{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/04/19/business/economy/19view.html |title=It May Be Time for the Fed to Go Negative |work=The New York Times |first=N. Gregory |last=Mankiw |author-link=N. Gregory Mankiw |date=18 April 2009 |archive-date=13 July 2025 |access-date=18 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250713091603/https://www.nytimes.com/2009/04/19/business/economy/19view.html |url-status=live }}</ref> though it was more of a thought experiment than a genuine proposal.
