The '''Turkish economic crisis''' ({{Langx|tr|Türkiye ekonomik krizi}}) is a [[Financial crisis|financial and economic crisis]] in [[economy of Turkey|Turkey]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Michaelson |first=Ruth |date=2023-05-16 |title=Turkey's economic crisis expected to deepen after Erdoğan tops poll |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/may/16/turkey-economic-crisis-expected-to-deepen-after-erdogan-tops-election-poll |access-date=2023-05-16 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> It is characterized by the [[Turkish lira]] (TRY) plunging in value, high [[inflation]], [[Fisher effect|rising borrowing costs]], and correspondingly rising [[Default (finance)|loan defaults]]. The crisis was caused by the Turkish economy's excessive [[Current account (balance of payments)|current account]] deficit and large amounts of private foreign-currency denominated debt.<ref name=e101 /><ref name=challenge /><ref name=crash /><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.caixinglobal.com/2018-08-19/turkeys-lessons-for-emerging-economies-101316583.html |title=Turkey's Lessons for Emerging Economies – Caixin Global |website=www.caixinglobal.com |language=en|access-date=20 August 2018|archive-date=28 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190428132328/https://www.caixinglobal.com/2018-08-19/turkeys-lessons-for-emerging-economies-101316583.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> 

Some analysts also stress the leveraging effects of the [[geopolitical]] frictions with the [[United States]]. Following the detention of American pastor [[Andrew Brunson]], who was arrested on espionage charges after the failed [[2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt]], the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] exerted pressure towards Turkey by imposing further sanctions. The economic sanctions therefore doubled the tariffs on Turkey, as imported steel rises up to 50% and on aluminum to 20%. As a result, Turkish steel was priced out of the US market, which previously amounted to 13% of Turkey's total steel exports.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 2019 |title=International Trade Administration |url=https://legacy.trade.gov/steel/countries/pdfs/exports-Turkey.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Goujon |first1=Reva |date=16 August 2018 |title=Making Sense of Turkey's Economic Crisis |url=https://worldview.stratfor.com/article/making-sense-turkeys-economic-crisis |work=Stratfor|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180816160000/https://worldview.stratfor.com/article/making-sense-turkeys-economic-crisis|archive-date=16 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/08/17/business/turkey-lira-currency.html |title=Life in Turkey Now: Tough Talk, but Fears of Drug Shortages |date=17 August 2018 |work=New York Times |author=Jack Ewing|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=7 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180907204158/https://www.nytimes.com/2018/08/17/business/turkey-lira-currency.html|url-status=live}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=October 2023}}

After a period of modest recovery in 2020 and early 2021 amid the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey|COVID-19 pandemic]], the Turkish lira plunged following the replacement of [[Central Bank of Turkey|Central Bank]] chief [[Naci Ağbal]] with [[Şahap Kavcıoğlu]],<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Spicer |first1=Jonathan Spicer |last2=Erkoyun |first2=Ezgi |date=2021-03-22 |title=Turkish lira plunges to near record low after Erdogan sacks central bank chief |work=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-cenbank-idUSKBN2BE0UF |accessdate=2021-10-25|archive-date=27 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211027052052/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-cenbank-idUSKBN2BE0UF|url-status=live}}</ref> who slashed interest rates from 19%<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kidera |first=Momoko |date=21 October 2021 |title=Turkey cuts interest rates again despite calls for course change |url=https://asia.nikkei.com/Economy/Turkey-cuts-interest-rates-again-despite-calls-for-course-change|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-22 |website=[[Nikkei Asia]] |language=en-GB|archive-date=25 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220125060725/https://asia.nikkei.com/Economy/Turkey-cuts-interest-rates-again-despite-calls-for-course-change}}</ref> to 14%.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2021-10-22 |title=Turkish lira drops to new all-time low after rates slashed |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/10/22/turkish-lira-drops-to-new-all-time-low-after-rates-slashed.html|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-24 |website=[[CNBC]] |language=en|archive-date=26 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126175837/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/10/22/turkish-lira-drops-to-new-all-time-low-after-rates-slashed.html}}</ref> The lira lost 44% of its value in 2021 alone.<ref>Turak, Natasha (13 January 2022). [https://www.cnbc.com/2022/01/13/erdogan-blames-turkeys-currency-woes-on-foreign-financial-tools-as-central-bank-reserves-fall.html Erdogan blames Turkey’s currency problems on ‘foreign financial tools’ as central bank reserves fall.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220510191011/https://www.cnbc.com/2022/01/13/erdogan-blames-turkeys-currency-woes-on-foreign-financial-tools-as-central-bank-reserves-fall.html |date=10 May 2022 }} ''CNBC.''</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/06/23/europe/turkey-istanbul-mayor-election-intl/index.html |title=Istanbul election rerun won by opposition, in blow to Erdogan |author=Isil Sariyuce and Ivana Kottasová |website=CNN |date=23 June 2019|access-date=20 August 2019|archive-date=29 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190829143116/https://www.cnn.com/2019/06/23/europe/turkey-istanbul-mayor-election-intl/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Gall |first=Carlotta |date=23 June 2019 |title=Turkey's President Suffers Stinging Defeat in Istanbul Election Redo |language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/06/23/world/europe/istanbul-mayor-election-erdogan.html|access-date=20 August 2019 |issn=0362-4331|archive-date=6 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190806102800/https://www.nytimes.com/2019/06/23/world/europe/istanbul-mayor-election-erdogan.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2023, however, Erdoğan began to follow orthodox banking methods under the guidance of [[Mehmet Şimşek]] and [[Hafize Gaye Erkan]]. The interest rate has stood at 50% since March 2024 upon the advice of [[Fatih Karahan]], the governor of the central bank who succeeded Erkan.<ref name="Interest rate unchanged" /> This contributed to the decline of inflation, since as of November 2024, inflation is at 47.09%, down from its all-time high of 83%.<ref name="November 2024 inflation" /> As of July 2026 the YoY inflation stood on 31.75%.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TCMB - Consumer Prices |url=https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/EN/TCMB+EN/Main+Menu/Statistics/Inflation+Data |access-date=2026-08-04 |website=www.tcmb.gov.tr |language=en}}</ref>   

More recently, political turmoil has further complicated the economic recovery. A series of anti-democratic crackdowns, including the high-profile detention of an Istanbul mayor and other opposition figures, have deepened market uncertainty and triggered sharp selloffs in equity markets.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Turak |first=Natasha |date=2025-03-24 |title=Political and financial turmoil set to dominate Turkey, risking economic stabilization plans |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2025/03/24/political-and-financial-turmoil-set-to-dominate-turkey-risking-economic-stabilization-plans.html |access-date=2025-03-26 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Buyuk |first=Hamdi Firat |date=2025-03-19 |title=Turkish Economy Takes Hit After Istanbul Mayor's Detention |url=https://balkaninsight.com/2025/03/19/turkish-economy-takes-hit-after-istanbul-mayors-detention/ |access-date=2025-03-26 |website=Balkan Insight |language=en-US}}</ref> These events have prompted both domestic and international policymakers to scramble: Finance Minister Mehmet Şimşek and central bank officials have engaged in calls with international investors,<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Spicer |first1=Jonathan |last2=Jones |first2=Marc |last3=George |first3=Libby |date=25 March 2025 |title=Turkey's Simsek seeks to calm investors, says market strains will be managed, sources say |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkeys-simsek-cenbank-governor-hold-call-with-international-investors-2025-03-25/ |access-date=26 March 2025 |work=Reuters}}</ref> while authorities have also taken measures such as banning short selling and relaxing buyback rules in an effort to stabilize the markets.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rahman |first=Fareed |title=Turkey bans short selling and eases buyback rules amid market rout |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/economy/2025/03/24/turkey-bans-short-selling-and-eases-buyback-rules-amid-market-rout/ |access-date=2025-03-26 |website=The National |language=en}}</ref> Meanwhile, rating agencies and international observers warn that the ongoing political repression may derail broader reform efforts and threaten Turkey's fragile economic stabilization.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Turkey's anti-democratic crackdown is damaging its economy |url=https://www.economist.com/europe/2025/03/24/turkeys-anti-democratic-crackdown-is-damaging-its-economy |access-date=2025-03-26 |newspaper=The Economist |issn=0013-0613}}</ref>

== Current account deficit and foreign-currency debt ==
{{Economy of Turkey}}
[[File:Türkiye'nin dış ticareti.png|thumb|Turkey's exports as percentage of imports]]
A longstanding characteristic of Turkey's economy is a low savings rate.<ref name=economist>{{cite news |url=https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2018/05/19/how-turkey-fell-from-investment-darling-to-junk-rated-emerging-market |title=How Turkey fell from investment darling to junk-rated emerging market |date=19 May 2018 |newspaper=The Economist|access-date=23 May 2018|archive-date=23 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190223151134/https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2018/05/19/how-turkey-fell-from-investment-darling-to-junk-rated-emerging-market|url-status=live}}</ref> Since [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] assumed control of the government, Turkey has been running huge and growing [[Current account (balance of payments)|current account]] deficits, $33.1 billion in 2016 and $47.3 billion in 2017,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkeys-current-account-deficit-at-5-4-billion-in-april-133114 |title=Turkey's current account deficit at $5.4 billion in April |date=11 June 2018 |work=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=28 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428070639/https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkeys-current-account-deficit-at-5-4-billion-in-april-133114|url-status=live}}</ref> climbing to US$7.1 billion in the month of January 2018 with the rolling 12-month deficit rising to $51.6 billion,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-economy/turkish-current-account-deficit-more-doubles |title=Turkish current account deficit more than doubles |date=12 March 2018 |work=Ahval|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612140422/https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-economy/turkish-current-account-deficit-more-doubles|url-status=dead}}</ref> one of the largest current account deficits in the world.<ref name=economist /> The economy has relied on capital inflows to fund private-sector excess, with Turkey's banks and big firms borrowing heavily, often in foreign currencies.<ref name=economist /> Under these conditions, Turkey must find approximately $200 billion a year to fund its wide current account deficit and maturing debt, while being always at risk of inflows drying up; the state has gross foreign currency reserves of just $85 billion.<ref name=challenge>{{cite web |url=https://www.ft.com/content/79317f20-67f5-11e8-8cf3-0c230fa67aec |title=Inflation rise poses challenge to Erdogan as election looms |date=5 June 2018 |work=Financial Times|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=8 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190408090707/https://www.ft.com/content/79317f20-67f5-11e8-8cf3-0c230fa67aec|url-status=live}}</ref> The economic policy underlying these trends had increasingly been micro-managed by Erdoğan since the election of his [[Justice and Development Party (Turkey)|Justice and Development Party]] (AKP) in 2002, and strongly so since 2008, with a focus on the [[construction|construction industry]], state-awarded contracts and stimulus measures. Although, [[research and development]] expenditure of the country (% of GDP){{How much|date=December 2018}} and the government expenditure on [[education]] (% of GDP){{How much|date=December 2018}} are nearly doubled during AKP governments, the desired outcomes could not be achieved<ref>{{cite web |title=Research and development expenditure (% of GDP) |url=https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/GB.XPD.RSDV.GD.ZS |website=The World Bank Data |publisher=UNESCO Institute for Statistics |access-date=31 October 2018 |archive-date=19 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190519013757/https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/GB.XPD.RSDV.GD.ZS |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Government expenditure on education, total (% of GDP) |url=https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SE.XPD.TOTL.GD.ZS?end=2014&locations=TR&start=1999&view=chart&year=2014 |publisher=United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization ( UNESCO ) Institute for Statistics. |access-date=31 October 2018 |archive-date=31 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181031132959/https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SE.XPD.TOTL.GD.ZS?end=2014&locations=TR&start=1999&view=chart&year=2014 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=bet>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/amp/news/articles/2018-06-22/a-crazy-200-billion-says-erdogan-wins-his-election-bet |title=A Crazy $200 Billion Says Erdogan Wins His Election Bet |date=22 June 2018 |publisher=Bloomberg L.P. |author1=Marc Champion |author2=Cagan Koc|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=21 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190421130408/https://www.bloomberg.com/amp/news/articles/2018-06-22/a-crazy-200-billion-says-erdogan-wins-his-election-bet|url-status=live}}</ref> The motive for these policies have been described as Erdoğan losing faith in Western-style capitalism since the [[2008 financial crisis]] by the secretary general of the main Turkish business association, [[Turkish Industry and Business Association|TUSIAD]].<ref name=bet /> Although not directly related in the conflict, the [[Operation Olive Branch|Turkish invasion of Afrin]] largely strained US-Turkish relations, and led to mass instability in Syria. This led to a global view of Turkey as an unnecessary aggressor.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.americanprogress.org/issues/security/news/2018/01/19/445271/potential-turkish-military-move-afrin-risks-wider-war/ |title=Potential Turkish Military Move on Afrin Risks Wider War |date=19 January 2018|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=17 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210517155658/https://www.americanprogress.org/issues/security/news/2018/01/19/445271/potential-turkish-military-move-afrin-risks-wider-war/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.brookings.edu/blog/order-from-chaos/2018/01/26/whats-next-for-turkey-the-us-and-the-ypg-after-the-afrin-operation/ |title=What's next for Turkey, the US, and the YPG after the Afrin operation? |date=26 January 2018|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=19 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180319214515/https://www.brookings.edu/blog/order-from-chaos/2018/01/26/whats-next-for-turkey-the-us-and-the-ypg-after-the-afrin-operation/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2018/feb/23/world-leaders-brutal-attack-kurdish-afrin-turkish-army |title=Why are world leaders backing this brutal attack against Kurdish Afrin? &#124; David Graeber |website=[[TheGuardian.com]] |date=23 February 2018|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=6 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211006142432/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2018/feb/23/world-leaders-brutal-attack-kurdish-afrin-turkish-army|url-status=live}}</ref>
[[File:Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge IMG 3065.jpg|thumb|Previous economic growth had been led by fiscal and monetary stimulus to the construction industry,<ref name=bentley /><ref name=bet /> resulting in a huge backlog of unsold new houses,<ref name=houses /> and unprofitable grand projects like the [[Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge]];<ref name=selim /> its operator is guaranteed 135k passenger car-equivalent of daily toll revenue.]]
Investment inflows had already been declining in the period leading up to the crisis, owing to Erdoğan instigating political disagreements with countries that were major sources of such inflows (such as Germany, France, and the Netherlands).<ref name=e101 /> Following the [[2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt|2016 coup attempt]], the government [[2016–present purges in Turkey|seized the assets]] of those it stated were involved, even if their ties to the coup were tenuous. Erdoğan has not taken seriously concerns that foreign companies investing in Turkey might be deterred by the country's political instability.<ref name=e101 /> Other factors include worries about the decreasing value of lira (TRY) which threatens to eat into investors' profit margins.<ref name=e101>{{cite web |url=https://foreignpolicy.com/2018/05/25/erdogan-is-a-mad-economist-and-turkey-is-his-laboratory/ |title=Erdogan Is Failing Economics 101 |date=25 May 2018 |publisher=Foreign Policy |author=Borzou Daragahi|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=14 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190414084916/https://foreignpolicy.com/2018/05/25/erdogan-is-a-mad-economist-and-turkey-is-his-laboratory/|url-status=live}}</ref> Investment inflows have also declined because Erdoğan's [[Erdoğanism|increasing authoritarianism]] has quelled free and factual reporting by [[financial analyst]]s in Turkey.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-24/a-big-chill-silences-turkey-s-market-analysts-amid-lira-s-plunge |title=A Big Chill Has Silenced Turkey's Market Analysts |newspaper=Bloomberg.com |date=24 May 2018 |publisher=Bloomberg|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=28 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180828192717/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-24/a-big-chill-silences-turkey-s-market-analysts-amid-lira-s-plunge|url-status=live}}</ref> Between January and May 2017, foreign portfolio investors funded $13.2 billion of Turkey's $17.5 billion current account deficit, according to the latest available data. During the same period in 2018, they plugged just $763 million of a swollen $27.3 billion deficit.<ref name=pariah />

By the end of 2017, the corporate foreign-currency debt in Turkey had more than doubled since 2009, up to $214 billion after netting against their foreign-exchange assets.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-03-29/turkey-s-bill-for-debt-fueled-economic-growth-starts-to-fall-due |title=Turkey's Bill for Debt-Fueled Economic Growth Starts to Fall Due |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=29 March 2018 |agency=Bloomberg|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=27 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180927134801/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-03-29/turkey-s-bill-for-debt-fueled-economic-growth-starts-to-fall-due|url-status=live}}</ref> Turkey's gross external debt, both public and private, stood at $453.2 billion at the end of 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/economy/turkeys-external-debt-stock-reaches-4532b-/1103634 |title=Turkey's external debt stock reaches $453.2B |date=30 March 2018 |agency=Anadolu|access-date=23 May 2018|archive-date=21 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180921121856/https://www.aa.com.tr/en/economy/turkeys-external-debt-stock-reaches-4532b-/1103634|url-status=live}}</ref> As of March 2018, $181.8 billion of external debt, public and private, was due to mature within a year.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/b19b5048-dd64-4075-ae01-47b2fd3ede50/st.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=ROOTWORKSPACE-b19b5048-dd64-4075-ae01-47b2fd3ede50-mdO36yX |title=Short Term External Debt Statistics |date=March 2018 |work=Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey)|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=28 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180528052619/http://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/b19b5048-dd64-4075-ae01-47b2fd3ede50/st.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=ROOTWORKSPACE-b19b5048-dd64-4075-ae01-47b2fd3ede50-mdO36yX|url-status=live}}</ref> Non-resident holdings of domestic shares stood at $53.3 billion in early March and at $39.6 billion in mid-May, and non-resident holdings of domestic government bonds stood at $32.0 billion in early March and at $24.7 billion in mid-May.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/7b1a6b8b-cd10-43ae-90b4-b3d702fae602/hmkexcelEn.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=ROOTWORKSPACE-7b1a6b8b-cd10-43ae-90b4-b3d702fae602-mehWrra/ |title=Securities Statistics |date=18 May 2018 |work=Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey)|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=13 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613160939/http://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/7b1a6b8b-cd10-43ae-90b4-b3d702fae602/hmkexcelEn.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=ROOTWORKSPACE-7b1a6b8b-cd10-43ae-90b4-b3d702fae602-mehWrra%2F|url-status=live}}</ref> Overall non-residents' ownership of Turkish equities, government bonds and corporate debt has plummeted from a high of $92 billion in August 2017 to just $53 billion as of 13 July 2018.<ref name=pariah>{{cite web |url=https://www.ft.com/content/115e91ac-8f51-11e8-bb8f-a6a2f7bca546 |title=Turkey nears 'pariah' status over defiance on rates |date=31 July 2018 |work=Financial Times|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=26 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826072355/https://www.ft.com/content/115e91ac-8f51-11e8-bb8f-a6a2f7bca546|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Government's 'action plans' to confront the crisis ==

In 2018, the finance minister of the Turkish government, Albayrak unveiled a new economic program to stave off the financial crisis. The three-year plan aims to "reign in inflation, spur growth and cut the current account deficit".<ref>{{cite web |title=Turkey unveils 2019–2021 economic programme |url=https://www.trtworld.com/turkey/turkey-unveils-2019-2021-economic-programme-20330 |publisher=TRT World |access-date=20 September 2018 |archive-date=31 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181031173913/https://www.trtworld.com/turkey/turkey-unveils-2019-2021-economic-programme-20330 |url-status=live}}</ref> The plan includes reduction on the government expenditures by $10 billion and suspension of the projects whose tender have not been carried out yet. The transformational phase of the plan will be focusing on value-added areas to increase the country's export volume and long-term production capacity with the goal of creating two million new jobs by 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=New economic program: Turkey lays out a broad guideline to rebalance economic growth |url=https://www.dailysabah.com/economy/2018/09/21/new-economic-program-turkey-lays-out-a-broad-guideline-to-rebalance-economic-growth-1537477046 |publisher=Daily Sabah |access-date=20 September 2018 |archive-date=21 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180921013106/https://www.dailysabah.com/economy/2018/09/21/new-economic-program-turkey-lays-out-a-broad-guideline-to-rebalance-economic-growth-1537477046 |url-status=live}}</ref> The program is expected to lower economic growth substantially in the short term (from a previous forecast of 5.5% to 3.8% in 2018 and 2.3% in 2019) but with a gradual growth increase by 2021 towards 5%.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Turkish government presents plan to balance the economy |date=20 September 2018 |url=https://www.bbva.com/en/the-turkish-government-presents-plan-to-balance-the-economy/ |publisher=BBVA |access-date=4 November 2018 |archive-date=4 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181104125924/https://www.bbva.com/en/the-turkish-government-presents-plan-to-balance-the-economy/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Turkey unveils plan to stave off economic crisis |url=https://www.dw.com/en/turkey-unveils-plan-to-stave-off-economic-crisis/a-45581306 |publisher=Deutsche Welle |access-date=31 October 2018 |archive-date=31 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181031133249/https://www.dw.com/en/turkey-unveils-plan-to-stave-off-economic-crisis/a-45581306 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Presidential interference with the central bank ==
{{Erdogan sidebar}}
Turkey has experienced substantially higher [[inflation]] than other [[emerging market]]s.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-turkey-emerging-yield/with-high-inflation-turkish-lira-lacks-yield-buffer-idUKKBN1CG1RX |title=With high inflation, Turkish lira lacks yield buffer |date=11 October 2017 |work=Reuters|access-date=23 May 2018|archive-date=28 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191128055707/https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-turkey-emerging-yield/with-high-inflation-turkish-lira-lacks-yield-buffer-idUKKBN1CG1RX|url-status=live}}</ref> In October 2017, inflation was at 11.9%, the highest rate since July 2008.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.handelsblatt.com/finanzen/maerkte/devisen-rohstoffe/tuerkische-lira-lira-faellt-richtung-rekordtief/20538184.html?ticket=ST-7210-45hD6rWiFYdVLkBpNMdq-ap1 |title=Lira fällt Richtung Rekordtief |publisher=[[Handelsblatt]] |date=3 November 2017|access-date=3 August 2018|archive-date=12 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190912182732/https://www.handelsblatt.com/finanzen/maerkte/devisen-rohstoffe/tuerkische-lira-lira-faellt-richtung-rekordtief/20538184.html?ticket=ST-43384805-adtybnAQpMaCUUYyQqHQ-ap2|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2018, the lira's exchange rate accelerated deterioration, reaching a level of 4.0 TRY per USD by late March, 4.5 TRY per USD by mid-May, 5.0 TRY per USD by early August and 6.0 as well as 7.0 TRY per USD by mid-August. Among economists, the accelerating loss of value was generally attributed to [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] preventing the [[Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey]] from making the necessary interest rate adjustments.<ref name=wapo>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wonk/wp/2018/05/16/turkeys-leader-is-helping-to-crash-its-currency/ |title=Turkey's leader is helping to crash its currency |date=16 May 2018 |newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=27 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180727140901/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wonk/wp/2018/05/16/turkeys-leader-is-helping-to-crash-its-currency/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ft.com/content/e41a56d6-5855-11e8-bdb7-f6677d2e1ce8 |title=Investors lose their appetite for Turkey |date=16 May 2018 |work=Financial Times|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=17 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180917124403/https://www.ft.com/content/e41a56d6-5855-11e8-bdb7-f6677d2e1ce8|url-status=live}}</ref>

Erdoğan, who said interest rates beyond his control to be "the mother and father of all evil",<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-currency/turkeys-erdogan-calls-interest-rates-mother-of-all-evil-lira-slides-idUSKBN1IC1NV |title=Turkey's Erdogan calls interest rates "mother of all evil"; lira slides |last1=Küçükgöçmen |first1=Ali |date=11 May 2018 |work=Reuters|access-date=9 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519111546/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-currency/turkeys-erdogan-calls-interest-rates-mother-of-all-evil-lira-slides-idUSKBN1IC1NV|archive-date=19 May 2018 |last2=Taner |first2=Behiye Selin |language=en-US}}</ref> shared his unorthodox interest rate theories in a 14 May interview with ''[[Bloomberg News|Bloomberg]]'' and said that "the central bank can't take this independence and set aside the signals given by the president."<ref name=wapo /><ref name=unorthodox>{{cite web |url=https://www.al-monitor.com/pulse/originals/2018/05/turkey-erdogans-controversial-economic-theory.html |title=The unorthodox theory behind Erdogan's monetary policy |date=25 May 2018 |publisher=Al-Monitor |author=Marc Edward Hoffman|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=21 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121181215/https://www.al-monitor.com/pulse/originals/2018/05/turkey-erdogans-controversial-economic-theory.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Presidential intervention with central bank policy comes with a general perception in international investment circles of a "textbook institutional decline" in Turkey, with Erdoğan seen increasingly reliant on politicians whose main qualifications for their jobs is loyalty, at the expense of more qualified and experienced options.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-18/why-investors-have-become-skittish-about-turkey |title=Why Investors Have Become Skittish About Turkey |date=18 May 2018 |publisher=Bloomberg|access-date=23 May 2018|archive-date=28 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191128203115/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-18/why-investors-have-become-skittish-about-turkey|url-status=live}}</ref> Erdoğan also has a long history of voicing [[Islamism|Islamist]] discourse of interest-based banking as "[[Haram|prohibited by Islam]]" and "a serious dead-end".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ft.com/content/9ef872ff-bfce-3db5-bc22-67c649327c2f |title=Turkish lira falls further as Erdogan calls for interest rate cuts |date=24 November 2016 |work=Financial Times|access-date=23 May 2018|archive-date=28 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191128120117/https://www.ft.com/content/9ef872ff-bfce-3db5-bc22-67c649327c2f|url-status=live|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/turkey-banks/rise-of-turkish-islamic-banks-chimes-with-erdogans-ideals-idUSL5N0WB3RW20150315 |title=Rise of Turkish Islamic banks chimes with Erdogan's ideals |last1=Toksabay |first1=Ece |last2=Dolan |first2=David |date=15 March 2015 |work=Reuters|access-date=23 May 2018|archive-date=28 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191128201757/https://www.reuters.com/article/turkey-banks/rise-of-turkish-islamic-banks-chimes-with-erdogans-ideals-idUSL5N0WB3RW20150315|url-status=live}}</ref> He is also on record referring to interest rate increases as "[[treason]]".<ref name=crash>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2018/07/13/turkeys-economy-looks-like-its-headed-big-crash/ |title=Turkey's economy looks like it's headed for a big crash |date=13 July 2018 |newspaper=Washington Post |author=Matt O'Brien|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=8 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190408090710/https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2018/07/13/turkeys-economy-looks-like-its-headed-big-crash/|url-status=live}}</ref> Despite Erdogan's opposition, Turkey's Central Bank made sharp interest rates increases.<ref>{{cite news |title=Defying Erdogan, Turkey's Central Bank Raises Interest Rates |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/09/13/business/turkey-central-bank-interest-rates-erdogan.html |work=The New York Times |date=13 September 2018 |access-date=13 September 2018 |last1=Alderman |first1=Liz |last2=Rao |first2=Prashant S. |archive-date=13 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180913144230/https://www.nytimes.com/2018/09/13/business/turkey-central-bank-interest-rates-erdogan.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

The ''[[Financial Times]]'' quoted leading emerging markets financial analyst Timothy Ash analyzing that "Turkey has strong banks, healthy public finances, good demographics, pro-business culture but [has been] spoiled over past four to five years by unorthodox and loose macroeconomic management."<ref name=strong /> By mid-June, analysts in London suggested that with its current government, Turkey would be well advised to seek an [[International Monetary Fund]] loan even before the dwindling central bank foreign exchange reserves run out, because it would strengthen the central bank's hand against Erdoğan and help gain back investor confidence in the soundness of Turkey's economic policies.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/turkey-needs-imf-loans-after-investor-confidence-undercut |title=Turkey needs IMF loans after investor confidence undercut |date=16 June 2018 |publisher=Ahval |author=Mark Bentley|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=29 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191129184012/https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/turkey-needs-imf-loans-after-investor-confidence-undercut|url-status=live}}</ref>

Economist [[Paul Krugman]] described the unfolding crisis as "a classic currency-and-debt crisis, of a kind we've seen many times", adding: "At such a time, the quality of leadership suddenly matters a great deal. You need officials who understand what's happening, can devise a response and have enough credibility that markets give them the benefit of the doubt. Some emerging markets have those things, and they are riding out the turmoil fairly well. The Erdoğan regime has none of that."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/05/24/opinion/turkey-trump-erdogan.html?action=click&pgtype=Homepage&clickSource=story-heading&module=opinion-c-col-left-region&region=opinion-c-col-left-region&WT.nav=opinion-c-col-left-region |title=Turmoil for Turkey's Trump |date=24 May 2018 |author=Paul Krugman |work=New York Times|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=28 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181128092742/https://www.nytimes.com/2018/05/24/opinion/turkey-trump-erdogan.html?action=click&pgtype=Homepage&clickSource=story-heading&module=opinion-c-col-left-region&region=opinion-c-col-left-region&WT.nav=opinion-c-col-left-region|url-status=live}}</ref>

In March 2021, Erdoğan fired Naci Ağbal, the governeor of the central bank. This led to shock in financial markets according to the Christian Science Monitor.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |title=Turkey shows why a central bank's independence is central |url=https://www.csmonitor.com/Commentary/the-monitors-view/2021/0322/Turkey-shows-why-a-central-bank-s-independence-is-central |access-date=2025-04-07 |work=Christian Science Monitor |issn=0882-7729}}</ref> In his stead, Erdoğan appointed a newspaper columnist who according to the Monitor agrees with Erdoğan's economic views.<ref name=":1" />

In August 2023, Turkey's central bank raised interest rates by 7.5 points to 25% to tackle inflation, signaling a shift from previous policies. President Erdoğan's new economics team aims to restore policy orthodoxy and stabilize the economy. Despite the positive currency response, the lira remains near historic lows.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Samson |first=Adam |date=2023-08-24|title= Turkey raises interest rates as it steps up decisive shift in economic policy |language=en |work=Financial Times |url= https://www.ft.com/content/5e5cc4e2-61bf-475c-bdaf-43a32fdaf459 |access-date=2023-08-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news  |date=2023-08-24|title= Turkey's central bank raises interest rates again in another sign of normalizing economic policy |language=en |work=Independent |url= https://www.independent.co.uk/news/recep-tayyip-erdogan-ap-turkey-ankara-merrill-lynch-b2398684.html |access-date=2023-08-31}}</ref>

== Consequences in Turkey ==
{{Update|timelines|date=August 2024}}
[[File:Recep Tayyip Erdogan WEF 2004.jpg|thumb|upright|right|[[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]]'s unorthodox views on interest rates are stated to be one of the most important causes of the crisis.<ref name=wapo /><ref name=e101 />]]
During the emergence of the crisis, lenders in Turkey were hit by restructuring demands of corporations unable to serve their [[United States dollar|USD]] or [[Euro|EUR]] denominated debt, due to the loss of value of their earnings in [[Turkish lira]]. While financial institutions had been the driver of the [[Borsa Istanbul|Istanbul stock exchange]] for many years, accounting for almost half its value, by mid-April they accounted for less than one-third.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-04-10/investors-bet-against-turkey-banks-as-debt-wave-gathers-force |title=Investors Bet Against Turkey Banks as Debt Wave Gains Force |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=10 April 2018 |agency=Bloomberg|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=24 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624065624/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-04-10/investors-bet-against-turkey-banks-as-debt-wave-gathers-force|url-status=live}}</ref> By late-May, lenders were facing a surge in demand from companies seeking to reorganise debt repayments.<ref name=pile>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-31/turkish-banks-face-increasing-pile-of-debt-restructuring-demands |title=Turkish Banks Face Rising Pile of Debt-Restructuring Demands |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=31 May 2018 |agency=Bloomberg|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=19 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180819085845/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-31/turkish-banks-face-increasing-pile-of-debt-restructuring-demands|url-status=live}}</ref> By early-July, public restructuring requests by some of the country's biggest businesses alone already totalled $20,000,000,000 with other debtors not publicly listed or large enough to require disclosures.<ref name=bereket>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-07-05/turkey-s-bereket-is-said-to-begin-sales-to-pay-4-billion-debt |title=Turkey's Bereket Is Said to Begin Sales to Pay $4 Billion Debt |date=5 July 2018 |publisher=Bloomberg|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=11 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911191219/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-07-05/turkey-s-bereket-is-said-to-begin-sales-to-pay-4-billion-debt|url-status=live}}</ref> The [[asset quality]] of Turkish banks, as well as their [[capital adequacy ratio]], kept deteriorating throughout the crisis.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/unethical-moodys-forewarns-second-wave-turkish-crisis |title='Unethical' Moody's forewarns second wave of Turkish crisis |date=9 June 2018 |author=Mark Bentley |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612140111/https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/unethical-moodys-forewarns-second-wave-turkish-crisis|url-status=dead}}</ref> By June [[Halkbank|Halk Bankası]], the most vulnerable of the large lenders, had lost 63% of its US dollar value since last summer and traded at 40% of book value.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://asiatimes.com/article/turkeys-economic-crisis-has-just-begun/ |title=Turkey's economic crisis has just begun |date=12 June 2018 |author=David P. Goldman |work=Asia Times}}</ref> However, it is hard to say that this is mainly due to the economic developments in Turkey since the valuation of Halkbank was largely affected by the rumors over the possible outcomes of the US investigation about the bank's stated help to Iran in evading US sanctions.<ref name="ING-Halkbank">{{cite web |last1=Smallwood |first1=Nicholas |title=Halkbank: What happens next? |url=https://think.ing.com/articles/turkish-bank-halkbank-posts-1q18-results/ |website=THINK – Economic and Financial Analysis |publisher=ING Bank |access-date=4 November 2018 |archive-date=30 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220130023154/https://think.ing.com/articles/turkish-bank-halkbank-posts-1q18-results/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Banks continuously heightened interest rates for business and consumer loans and [[mortgage loan]] rates, towards 20% annually, thus curbing demand from businesses and consumers. With a corresponding growth in deposits, the gap between total deposits and total loans, which had been one of the highest in emerging markets, began to narrow.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-banking/cash-hungry-turkish-banks-raise-rates-highest-crisis |title=Cash-hungry Turkish banks raise rates to highest since crisis |date=9 April 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=23 May 2018|archive-date=24 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180524090403/https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-banking/cash-hungry-turkish-banks-raise-rates-highest-crisis|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=estate>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkey-limits-real-estate-commissions-house-prices-slashed |title=Turkey limits real estate commissions, house prices slashed |date=14 May 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612144822/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkey-limits-real-estate-commissions-house-prices-slashed|url-status=dead}}</ref> Nevertheless, this development has also led to incomplete or unoccupied housing and commercial real estate littering the outskirts of Turkey's major cities, as Erdoğan's policies had fuelled the construction sector, where many of his business allies are very active, to lead past economic growth.<ref name=bentley>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-elections/turkish-real-estate-ills-reflect-erdogans-snap-poll-decision |title=Turkish real estate ills reflect Erdoğan's snap poll decision |date=19 April 2018 |publisher=Ahval |author=Mark Bentley|access-date=27 August 2018|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612141619/https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-elections/turkish-real-estate-ills-reflect-erdogans-snap-poll-decision|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=estate /> In March 2018, home sales fell 14% and mortgage sales declined 35% compared to a year earlier. As of May, Turkey had around 2,000,000 unsold houses, a backlog three times the size of the average annual number of new housing sales.<ref name=houses>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/turkey-economy-realestate/turkish-property-firms-to-slash-prices-in-one-month-drive-to-revive-market-idUSL5N1SM2LT |title=Turkish property firms to slash prices in one-month drive to revive market |date=15 May 2018 |work=Reuters|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=29 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180929115143/https://www.reuters.com/article/turkey-economy-realestate/turkish-property-firms-to-slash-prices-in-one-month-drive-to-revive-market-idUSL5N1SM2LT|url-status=live}}</ref> In the first half of 2018, unsold stock of new housing kept increasing, while increases in new home prices in Turkey were lagging consumer price inflation by more than 10 percentage points.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-property/turkish-house-prices-lag-inflation-10-percentage-points |title=Turkish house prices lag inflation by 10 percentage points |date=17 July 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=17 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180717153932/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-property/turkish-house-prices-lag-inflation-10-percentage-points|url-status=dead}}</ref>

While heavy portfolio capital outflows persisted, $883,000,000 in June, with official foreign exchange reserves declining by a $6,990,000,000 during June, the current account deficit started narrowing in June, due to the weakened exchange rate for the lira. This was perceived as a sign of getting balanced economy.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkey-current-account-gap-narrows-sign-rebalancing |title=Turkey current account gap narrows in sign of rebalancing |date=10 August 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=10 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810142925/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkey-current-account-gap-narrows-sign-rebalancing|url-status=dead}}</ref> Turkish Lira started recover its losses as of September 2018 and the current account deficit continued to shrink.<ref name="Ahval-LiraGains">{{cite web |title=Turkish current account deficit narrows; lira gains |work=Ahval |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/turkish-current-account-deficit-narrows-lira-gains |publisher=Ahval News |access-date=14 September 2018 |archive-date=4 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181104130005/https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/turkish-current-account-deficit-narrows-lira-gains |url-status=live}}</ref>

As a consequence of the earlier [[monetary policy]] of easy money, any newfound fragile short-term macroeconomic stability is based on higher interest rates, thus creating a recessionary effect for the Turkish economy.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-contraction-looms-rates-fallout-becomes-evident |title=Turkish contraction looms as rates fallout becomes evident |date=8 June 2018 |publisher=Ahval |author=Güldem Atabay Şanlı|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612141715/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-contraction-looms-rates-fallout-becomes-evident|url-status=dead}}</ref> In mid-June, the ''[[Washington Post]]'' carried the quote from a senior financial figure in Istanbul that "years of irresponsible policies have overheated the Turkish economy. High inflation rates and current account deficits are going to prove sticky. I think we are at the end of our rope."<ref name=housing>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/worldviews/wp/2018/06/19/the-quest-to-defeat-erdogan/ |title=The quest to defeat Erdogan |date=19 June 2018 |newspaper=Washington Post |author=Ishaan Tharoor|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=22 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322023706/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/worldviews/wp/2018/06/19/the-quest-to-defeat-erdogan/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Suicides===
In January 2018, a worker [[self-immolated]] in front of [[TBMM|Parliament]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Meclis önünde kendini yakan işçi konuştu: Oyumu Tayyip'e attım |url=https://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/haber/meclis-onunde-kendini-yakan-isci-konustu-oyumu-tayyipe-attim-904439 |access-date=22 March 2021 |publisher=[[Cumhuriyet]] |language=tr |archive-date=22 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422201437/https://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/haber/meclis-onunde-kendini-yakan-isci-konustu-oyumu-tayyipe-attim-904439 |url-status=live}}</ref>. 

In February 2020, Adem Yarıcı, 42, who was unemployed for a long time, burnt himself infront of the office of the governor of Hatay, screaming "my children are hungry" on 7 February 2020; he later died.<ref>{{cite news |title='Çocuklarım aç' diyerek valilik önünde kendini yakan adam hayatını kaybetti! |url=https://tele1.com.tr/valilik-onunde-cocuklarim-ac-diyerek-kendini-yakti-127385 |access-date=22 March 2021 |work=Tele1 |language=tr |archive-date=26 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126055927/https://tele1.com.tr/valilik-onunde-cocuklarim-ac-diyerek-kendini-yakti-127385/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The Hatay governorship stated that he had received assistance from social services, and suffered from psychological problems.<ref>{{Cite web|title="Çocuklarım aç" diyerek kendini yakan baba hayatını kaybetti|url=https://t24.com.tr/haber/hatay-da-uzun-suredir-issiz-kalan-bir-kisi-cocuklarim-ac-diyerek-kendini-yakti,859770|website=T24|access-date=2026-01-28|language=Turkish}}</ref>

In November 2019 four siblings were found dead in an apartment in [[Fatih]], [[Istanbul]], having committed suicide because they were unable to pay their bills. The price of electricity increased in 2019 around 57% and youth unemployment stood around 27%. The electricity bill for the apartment had not been paid for several months.<ref name="suicides">{{cite news |last1=Shafak |first1=Elif |title=Family suicides in Turkey speak of a society that has lost hope |url=http://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2019/nov/13/family-suicides-turkey-society-lost-hope |access-date=9 December 2019 |work=The Guardian |archive-date=8 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191208152817/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2019/nov/13/family-suicides-turkey-society-lost-hope |url-status=live}}</ref>
 	
A family of four including two children 9 and 5 years old was similarly found in [[Antalya]]. A note left behind detailed the financial difficulties the family was experiencing.<ref name="suicides"/><ref name=guardian>{{cite news |title='Call me Robin Hood': mystery patron pays debts of Istanbul's poor |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/nov/18/call-me-robin-hood-mystery-patron-pays-debts-of-istanbul-poorest |date=18 November 2019 |access-date=30 January 2022 |archive-date=22 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122140816/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/nov/18/call-me-robin-hood-mystery-patron-pays-debts-of-istanbul-poorest |url-status=live}}</ref>

In mid-November ''The Guardian'' reported that an anonymous benefactor had paid off some debts at local grocery stores in [[Tuzla, Istanbul|Tuzla]] and left envelopes of cash on doorstops after the suicides.<ref name=guardian />
 	
[[AK Parti]] officials and media have denied that the recent deaths were caused by the rising cost of living.<ref name="suicides"/><ref name=guardian />

=== Collapse of birth rates ===
The collapse of birth rates in Turkey have been attributed to the ongoing economic crisis. The [[total fertility rate]] (TFR) dropped from 2.00 in 2018 to 1.48 in 2024, with 937,599 live births recorded that year. Persistent inflation, rising housing costs, job insecurity, and declining real incomes have been cited as the reasons for the collapse.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-27 |title=Turkey sounds alarm over declining birth rates amid economic concerns - Nordic Monitor |url=https://nordicmonitor.com/2025/05/turkey-sounds-alarm-over-declining-birth-rates-amid-economic-concerns/ |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=nordicmonitor.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Timeline of events (2018) ===
* 12 February – [[Yıldız Holding]] unexpectedly requested to restructure as much as $7,000,000,000 in loans.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-02-12/yildiz-7-billion-request-adds-to-asset-woes-for-turkish-banks |title=Yildiz $7 Billion Restructuring Bid Adds to Turkish Bank Woes |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=12 February 2018 |agency=Bloomberg|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612143719/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-02-12/yildiz-7-billion-request-adds-to-asset-woes-for-turkish-banks|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 21 February – Cemil Ertem, senior economic adviser to President [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]], published an opinion piece in the ''[[Daily Sabah]]'' suggesting that the [[International Monetary Fund|IMF]]'s policy advice for Turkey's central bank to raise short term interest rates should be ignored and that "not only Turkey, but all developing countries, should do the opposite of what the IMF preaches."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/imf-turkey/imf-backed-terrorists-has-failed-turkey-adviser |title=IMF backed by terrorists has failed in Turkey – adviser |date=21 February 2018 |work=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=13 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613162507/https://ahvalnews.com/imf-turkey/imf-backed-terrorists-has-failed-turkey-adviser|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 5 April – [[Mehmet Şimşek]], the Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the economy, sought to resign due to disagreement with Erdoğan about the latter's interference with central bank policy; but was later convinced to withdraw his resignation.<ref name=monitor>{{cite web |url=https://www.al-monitor.com/pulse/originals/2018/04/rumors-mehmet-simsek-resigns.html |title=Rumors of Turkish deputy PM's departure spook markets |date=5 April 2018 |publisher=Al-Monitor|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=9 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209081258/https://www.al-monitor.com/pulse/originals/2018/04/rumors-mehmet-simsek-resigns.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 7 April – [[Doğuş Group|Doğuş Holding]] applied to their banks for [[debt restructuring]]. Doğuş' outstanding loans stood at the equivalent of 23,500,000,000 Turkish lira (£2,765,597,500) at the end of 2017; up 11% from the year before.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-dogus-gyo-debt/turkeys-dogus-in-talks-with-banks-on-debt-restructuring-sources-idUSKBN1HE06U |title=Turkey's Dogus in talks with banks on debt restructuring |date=7 April 2018 |work=Reuters|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=18 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181118165116/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-dogus-gyo-debt/turkeys-dogus-in-talks-with-banks-on-debt-restructuring-sources-idUSKBN1HE06U|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 18 April – Erdoğan announced that the upcoming [[2018 Turkish general election|general election]] would be held on 24 June, eighteen months earlier than scheduled.
* 14 and 15 May – In a televised interview with ''Bloomberg'' and in a meeting with global money managers in [[London]], Erdoğan said that after the elections, he intended to take greater control of the economy, including ''de facto'' control over monetary policy, and to implement lower interest rates; this caused "shock and disbelief" among investors about the central bank's ability to fight inflation and stabilise the lira.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-markets-investors/disbelief-investors-in-turkey-stunned-by-erdogans-fight-with-markets-idUSKCN1IG2Y1 |title='Disbelief': Investors in Turkey stunned by Erdogan's fight with markets |date=15 May 2018 |work=Reuters|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=9 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709204527/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-markets-investors/disbelief-investors-in-turkey-stunned-by-erdogans-fight-with-markets-idUSKCN1IG2Y1|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=unorthodox />
* 23 May – Foreign exchange bureaus in [[Istanbul]] temporarily stopped trading amidst an extreme dive in the price of the lira.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/istanbul-foreign-exchange-bureaus-close-survive-turbulence |title=Istanbul foreign exchange bureaus close to survive turbulence |date=23 May 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=23 May 2018|archive-date=7 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180707122958/https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/istanbul-foreign-exchange-bureaus-close-survive-turbulence|url-status=dead}}</ref> On the same day, the [[Turkish Statistical Institute]] reported another slip in consumer confidence over the month of May, with all sub-indices decreasing. On 25 May 2018, it reported a sharp drop in confidence in Turkey's services, retail trade, and construction sectors over the month of May.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkeys-sectoral-confidence-goes-down-in-may-132348 |title=Turkey's sectoral confidence goes down in May |date=25 May 2018 |work=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=31 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180731124021/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkeys-sectoral-confidence-goes-down-in-may-132348|url-status=live}}</ref> Also on the same day, the [[Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey|Central Bank of Turkey]] raised interest rates at an emergency meeting of its Monetary Policy Committee, bowing to pressure from financial markets. The central bank raised its late liquidity window rate by 300 basis points to 16.5%.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-23/turkey-central-bank-has-held-extraordinary-rate-meeting |title=Turkey Raises Interest Rates to Halt Slide into Currency Crisis |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=23 May 2018 |agency=Bloomberg|access-date=23 May 2018|archive-date=23 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180623143111/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-23/turkey-central-bank-has-held-extraordinary-rate-meeting|url-status=live}}</ref> Taken against the vociferous objections of Erdoğan, this step brought temporary relief for the lira exchange rate.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wonk/wp/2018/05/25/turkey-tried-to-save-its-currency-it-worked-for-a-day/ |title=Turkey tried to save its currency. It worked – for a day. |date=25 May 2018 |newspaper=Washington Post |author=Matt O'Brien|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=9 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709064811/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wonk/wp/2018/05/25/turkey-tried-to-save-its-currency-it-worked-for-a-day/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 28 May – Turkey's central bank announced an operational simplification of its monetary policy, effective 1 June, coming with the announcement of another interest rate hike. The one-week repo rate, at 8 percent—currently not used—is to be raised to 16.5 percent and become the future benchmark of monetary policy. The current benchmark late liquidity window rate, now at 16.5 percent, will be fixed at 150 basis points above the one-week repo rate, which would now be 18 percent. The lira somewhat firmed in response.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-central-bank/turkish-central-bank-simplifies-policy-lira-gains |title=Turkish central bank simplifies policy; lira gains |date=28 May 2018 |work=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612141617/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-central-bank/turkish-central-bank-simplifies-policy-lira-gains|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-central-bank-says-it-will-complete-policy-simplification-132463 |title=Turkish Central Bank says it will complete 'policy simplification' |date=28 May 2018 |work=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=28 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180528124818/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-central-bank-says-it-will-complete-policy-simplification-132463|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 30 May – The Turkish Statistical Institute reported economic confidence sliding steeply in May to a value of 93.5, the lowest level in 15 months, since the aftermath of the [[2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt|2016 coup attempt]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-economic-confidence-slumps-lowest-15-months |title=Turkish economic confidence slumps to lowest in 15 months |date=30 May 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180812061818/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-economic-confidence-slumps-lowest-15-months|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 30 May – GAMA Holding sought to ease repayment terms for $1.5 billion of loans with creditors.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-banking/gama-refinancing-15-billion-latest-turkish-debt-applicant |title=Gama refinancing $1.5 billion latest Turkish debt applicant |date=30 May 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612141713/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-banking/gama-refinancing-15-billion-latest-turkish-debt-applicant|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 30 May – Turkey's central bank released minutes of the crucial 23 May Monetary Policy Committee meeting, saying that "the tight stance in monetary policy will be maintained decisively until the inflation outlook displays a significant improvement and becomes consistent with the targets", the latter being 5 percent by law.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-central-bank-vows-tight-policy-warns-about-risks-132659 |title=Turkish Central Bank vows tight policy, warns about risks |date=31 May 2018 |work=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612135855/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-central-bank-vows-tight-policy-warns-about-risks-132659|url-status=live}}</ref>

* 1 June – The Istanbul Chamber of Industry published its index of manufacturing in Turkey for the month of May, stating that with a sharp drop for the second consecutive month, manufacturing conditions deteriorated to the worst since 2009, elaborating that "inflationary pressures remained marked in May, cost burdens continued to rise in the manufacturing sector."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.markiteconomics.com/Survey/PressRelease.mvc/eca3dc09ed4a4ff592ec19620a507f1b |title=PMI posts 46.4 during May |date=1 June 2018 |work=Istanbul Chamber of Industry|access-date=27 August 2018|archive-date=12 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200312124708/https://www.markiteconomics.com/Survey/PressRelease.mvc/eca3dc09ed4a4ff592ec19620a507f1b|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 4 June – Turkey's statistics institute reported the annual inflation rate for May as risen to 12.2 percent from 10.9 percent the previous month, just below a 14-year high of last November, while monthly inflation was 1.6 percent.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-06-04/turkish-inflation-accelerates-more-than-expected-on-weak-lira |title=Turkey Inflation Accelerates in May on Weak Currency |date=4 June 2018 |publisher=Bloomberg|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=29 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180629211319/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-06-04/turkish-inflation-accelerates-more-than-expected-on-weak-lira|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloombergquint.com/onweb/2018/06/05/enthusiastic-lira-bulls-may-preclude-a-central-bank-rate-hike |title=Lira's Rebound From a Record May Preclude Central Bank Rate Hike |date=5 June 2018 |publisher=Bloomberg|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180812052758/https://www.bloombergquint.com/onweb/2018/06/05/enthusiastic-lira-bulls-may-preclude-a-central-bank-rate-hike|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 6 June – At the [[Borsa Istanbul]], Turkey's main stock index BIST-100 dropped 1.5 percent to the lowest level in dollar terms since the [[2008 financial crisis]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-stocks/turkish-stock-market-hits-lowest-2008-crisis |title=Turkish stock market hits lowest since 2008 crisis |date=6 June 2018 |work=Ahval|access-date=27 August 2018|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612162057/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-stocks/turkish-stock-market-hits-lowest-2008-crisis|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 7 June – Turkey's central bank at its regular Monetary Policy Committee meeting raised its benchmark repo rate by 125 basis points to 17.75 percent. The move beat market expectations, resulting in immediate gains for the lira, and the yield on the benchmark 10-year lira bond eased, after touching a record-high 15.41 percent on 6 June.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-06-07/turkish-central-bank-unexpectedly-raises-rate-to-17-75-percent |title=Turkey Central Bank Is Latest to Surprise With Big Rate Move |date=7 June 2018 |publisher=Bloomberg|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=23 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180623182432/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-06-07/turkish-central-bank-unexpectedly-raises-rate-to-17-75-percent|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 10 June – Turkey's Automotive Manufacturers Association published data for the month of May, showing car sales sliding to the lowest level since 2014. Passenger car sales slumped by 13 percent when compared to May 2017, while sales of commercial vehicles dropped 19 percent.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-car-sales-lowest-4-years-show-economic-woes |title=Turkish car sales at lowest in 4 years show economic woes |date=11 June 2018 |work=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612144631/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-car-sales-lowest-4-years-show-economic-woes|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 11 June – Turkey's central bank released financial data for April, with the account deficit widening by $1.7 billion to $5.4 billion.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-current-account-gap-widens-portfolio-inflows-slump |title=Turkish current account gap widens; portfolio inflows slump |date=11 June 2018 |work=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612143317/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-current-account-gap-widens-portfolio-inflows-slump|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 13 June – Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's senior economic adviser Cemil Ertem in an opinion piece in the ''Daily Sabah'' said that the unorthodox idea that it would be wrong to see inflation as a monetary phenomenon,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/erdogan-adviser-says-high-growth-doesnt-cause-inflation |title=Erdoğan adviser says high growth doesn't cause inflation |date=13 June 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=13 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613183937/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/erdogan-adviser-says-high-growth-doesnt-cause-inflation|url-status=dead}}</ref> leading to a sharp slide in the value of the lira and of Turkey's benchmark 10-year lira bonds, with yields on the latter reaching a record-high of 16.25 percent.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/turkish-lira-slumps-renewed-concern-over-economic-policy |title=Turkish lira slumps on renewed concern over economic policy |date=13 June 2018 |work=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=8 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180908211122/https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/turkish-lira-slumps-renewed-concern-over-economic-policy|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-06-13/turkey-s-bonds-lira-slide-a-third-day-before-central-banks-meet |title=Turkish Yields Head for Record While Lira Loses Rate-Hike Boost |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=13 June 2018 |agency=Bloomberg|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=13 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613184053/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-06-13/turkey-s-bonds-lira-slide-a-third-day-before-central-banks-meet|url-status=live}}</ref>[[File:DollarTRYCurrency.jpg|thumb|The Turkish Lira regained a significant proportion of its losses within the three months after July 2018. According to the models by IMF and International Institute of Finance made at the time, the lira was getting closer to the fair value but was still slightly undervalued.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bentley |first1=Mark |title=What next for Turkey after currency crisis? |url=https://www.spreaker.com/user/ahvalpod/what-next-for-turkey-after-currency-cris |publisher=Speaker |access-date=4 November 2018 |archive-date=17 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190117070108/https://www.spreaker.com/user/ahvalpod/what-next-for-turkey-after-currency-cris |url-status=dead}}</ref>]]
*14 June – Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in a televised interview said that his government would "conduct an operation against" international credit ratings agency [[Moody's Investors Service]] following elections on 24 June.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/erdogan-says-will-sanction-moodys-after-it-defamed-turkey |title=Erdoğan says will sanction Moody's after it defamed Turkey |date=14 June 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=15 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615012627/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/erdogan-says-will-sanction-moodys-after-it-defamed-turkey|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/turkey-currency/turkish-lira-weakens-market-seems-to-shrug-off-erdogans-comments-on-moodys-idUKL8N1TG2RB |title=Turkish lira weakens, market seems to shrug off Erdogan's comments on Moody's |date=14 June 2018 |work=Reuters|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=15 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615004821/https://uk.reuters.com/article/turkey-currency/turkish-lira-weakens-market-seems-to-shrug-off-erdogans-comments-on-moodys-idUKL8N1TG2RB|url-status=dead}}</ref> The next day, the lira finished its worst week since 2008, tumbling 5.7 per cent relative to the dollar, while also hitting its worst weekend close ever at US$4.73/TRY.<ref name="strong">{{cite web |url=https://www.ft.com/content/1e5f9fc6-7076-11e8-92d3-6c13e5c92914 |title=Turkish lira slides almost 6% in worst week in a decade |date=15 June 2018 |work=Financial Times|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=24 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624220804/https://www.ft.com/content/1e5f9fc6-7076-11e8-92d3-6c13e5c92914|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 24 June – In the [[2018 Turkish general election|Turkish general election]], Erdoğan retained the office of president while his [[Justice and Development Party (Turkey)|Justice and Development Party]] (AKP) narrowly lost its majority in parliament but achieved such majority together with its alliance partner the [[Nationalist Movement Party]] (MHP). The day after, the Turkish Industry and Business Association (TÜSİAD) urgently called for economic reforms.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkeys-top-business-group-calls-for-urgent-reforms-after-election-133769 |title=Turkey's top business group calls for 'urgent' reforms after election |date=25 June 2018 |work=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=27 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180627091320/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkeys-top-business-group-calls-for-urgent-reforms-after-election-133769|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 28 June – The Turkish Statistical Institute reported its economic confidence index dropping in June for the fifth straight month, with construction sector confidence leading the declines.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-economic-confidence-lowest-18-months |title=Turkish economic confidence lowest in 18 months |date=28 June 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=28 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180628152929/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-economic-confidence-lowest-18-months|url-status=dead}}</ref>

* 3 July – The Turkish Statistical Institute reported that Turkey's annual inflation rate surged to 15.4 percent in June, the highest level since 2003. Consumer price inflation climbed 2.6 percent month-on-month in June, exceeding annual price increases in many developed economies. Turkey's annual inflation rate now was about four times the average in emerging markets. Producer price increases accelerated to 23.7 percent from 20.2 percent the previous month.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-inflation-surges-highest-2003 |title=Turkish inflation surges to highest since 2003 |date=3 July 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=3 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180703221704/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-inflation-surges-highest-2003|url-status=dead}}</ref> On the same day, the Automotive Distributors Association said that sales of the commercial vehicles sank 44 percent in June from June 2017, while car sales fell 38 percent.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-car-sales-slump-underscoring-economic-slowdown |title=Turkish car sales slump, underscoring economic slowdown |date=3 July 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=3 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180703190914/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-car-sales-slump-underscoring-economic-slowdown|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 5 July – ''Bloomberg'' reported that Turkish and international banks were taking control of [[Türk Telekom]], Turkey's biggest telephone company, due to billions of dollars in unpaid debt. Creditors set up a special purpose vehicle to acquire the company as they try to resolve Turkey's biggest-ever debt default.<ref name=Telekom>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-07-04/banks-said-poised-to-take-over-majority-stake-in-turk-telekom |title=Banks Are Poised to Take a Majority Stake in Turk Telekom |date=5 July 2018 |publisher=Bloomberg|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=11 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911012813/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-07-04/banks-said-poised-to-take-over-majority-stake-in-turk-telekom|url-status=live}}</ref> The same day, Bereket Enerji group was reported seeking buyers for two power plants as it negotiates with banks to refinance $4 billion in debt.<ref name=bereket />
* 9 July – Erdoğan appointed his son-in-law [[Berat Albayrak]] as economic chief of his new administration, in charge of a new ministry of treasury and finance. Erdoğan also appointed Mustafa Varank, a close adviser who had overseen a pro-government social media team on Twitter and elsewhere, to industry minister, the other key economy portfolio.<ref name=Varank /> These announcement fueled investor unease about competence and orthodoxy of economic policymaking, with the [[Turkish lira]] losing 3.8 percent of its value within one hour after Albayrak's appointment.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-07-09/turkish-lira-slumps-after-names-son-in-law-as-economy-dzar |title=Turkish Lira Slumps as Erdogan Names Son-in-Law as Economy Chief |publisher=Bloomberg L.P. |date=9 July 2018|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=4 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404195915/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-07-09/turkish-lira-slumps-after-names-son-in-law-as-economy-dzar|url-status=live}}</ref> Same day, Erdoğan by presidential decree appropriated to himself the authority to appoint the central bank governor, his deputies and the monetary policy committee members.<ref name=Fadi>{{cite web |url=https://time.com/5343999/turkey-erdogan-economic-crisis/ |title=Turkey Is Heading for Economic Meltdown |date=20 July 2018 |publisher=TIME |author1=Fadi Hakura|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=24 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201124100150/https://time.com/5343999/turkey-erdogan-economic-crisis/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 11 July – The lira dropped 2.5 percent to 4.82 per dollar, its weakest level since falling to an all-time low of 4.92 against the U.S. currency in May. The stock market in Istanbul dropped 5.2 percent to 91.290 points. Yields on government debt surged.<ref name=Varank>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/turkish-lira-slides-towards-record-erdogan-tightens-grip |title=Turkish lira slides towards record as Erdoğan tightens grip |publisher=Ahval |date=11 July 2018|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=11 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180711230306/https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/turkish-lira-slides-towards-record-erdogan-tightens-grip|url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, the lira touched an all-time low of 4.98 lira for a US dollar.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/lira/istanbul-exchange-offices-stop-selling-dollars |title=Istanbul exchange offices stop selling dollars |publisher=Bloomberg L.P. |date=15 July 2018|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180712184312/https://ahvalnews.com/lira/istanbul-exchange-offices-stop-selling-dollars|url-status=dead}}</ref> Two days later, the lira recorded its biggest weekly slump in almost a decade. The benchmark Borsa Istanbul 100 Index fell the most since the foiled coup in 2016, with the selloff dragging price-to-estimated earnings valuations to the lowest in more than nine years. The 10-year government bond yield surged almost 100 basis points this week.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-07-13/lira-heads-for-steepest-drop-in-almost-10-years-in-week-of-drama |title=Lira Heads for Steepest Drop in Almost 10 Years in Week of Drama |publisher=Ahval |date=12 July 2018|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=14 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190414040529/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-07-13/lira-heads-for-steepest-drop-in-almost-10-years-in-week-of-drama|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 19 July – ÇEL-MER Çelik Endüstrisi, a leading Turkish steel producer also operating in the automobile sector, agriculture, white goods, machinery production and the defence industry, sought bankruptcy protection from the courts after it failed to repay its debts.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/top-turkish-steel-company-seeks-bankruptcy-protection |title=Top Turkish steel company seeks bankruptcy protection |publisher=Ahval |date=19 July 2018|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=19 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180719203409/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/top-turkish-steel-company-seeks-bankruptcy-protection|url-status=dead}}</ref>
