* 31 July – Turkey's central bank acknowledged it will not meet its 5 percent inflation target for three more years, disappointing investors seeking signs that monetary policy would tighten. Although Governor Murat Cetinkaya pledged to raise borrowing costs when needed, he predicted 13.4 percent inflation through this year, 9.3 percent through 2019 and 6.7 percent by the end of 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-07-31/turkey-admits-to-three-more-years-of-missing-inflation-target |title=Turkey Admits to 3 More Years of Missing Inflation Target |date=31 July 2018 |publisher=Bloomberg|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=1 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180801031554/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-07-31/turkey-admits-to-three-more-years-of-missing-inflation-target|url-status=live}}</ref> The same day, the Turkish lira heading for its longest streak of monthly losses since an International Monetary Fund bailout in 2001, the Banks Association of Turkey (TBB) drew up a framework of principles for restructuring loans that exceed 50 million lira: If lenders with exposure to at least 75 percent of the total owed agree, a committee of lenders should order measures such as changes to shareholder structure and management, asset sales, spinoffs and capital injections, resolving restructurings within 150 days.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-07-31/turkey-banks-want-faster-loan-restructuring-as-lira-plunge-bites |title=Turkey Banks Want Faster Loan Restructuring as Lira Plunge Bites |date=31 July 2018 |publisher=Bloomberg|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=1 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180801150503/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-07-31/turkey-banks-want-faster-loan-restructuring-as-lira-plunge-bites|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 1 August – Due to the weakening lira, Turkey's state pipeline operator [[BOTAŞ]] raised the price of natural gas used by electric power plants by 50 percent. BOTAŞ also raised natural gas prices for residential use. The same day, the energy regulation authority raised electricity prices for industrial and residential use.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nasdaq.com/article/turkeys-botas-hikes-natural-gas-price-for-power-generation-by-50-pct-20180731-01501 |title=Turkey's Botas hikes natural gas price for power generation by 50 pct |date=31 July 2018 |work=Nasdaq|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=1 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180801034336/https://www.nasdaq.com/article/turkeys-botas-hikes-natural-gas-price-for-power-generation-by-50-pct-20180731-01501|url-status=live}}</ref> Also the same day, the Istanbul Chamber of Industry said in a monthly survey of manufacturers that producer price inflation in July accelerated to the highest pace in more than a decade, after already having accelerated to 23.7 percent in June due to the Erdoğan government stimulating economic growth with a series of measures ahead of elections on 24 June.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-inflation/turkish-manufacturers-signal-more-bad-news-inflation |title=Turkish manufacturers signal more bad news for inflation |date=1 August 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=1 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180801130545/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-inflation/turkish-manufacturers-signal-more-bad-news-inflation|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 3 August – The Turkish Statistical Institute reported that Turkey's annual inflation rate increased to 15.9 percent, from 15.4 percent in June, extending the highest level since 2003. Producer price inflation climbed to 25 percent from 23.7 percent in June.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-inflation-accelerates-159-percent |title=Turkish inflation accelerates to 15.9 percent |date=3 August 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=3 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180803194124/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-inflation-accelerates-159-percent|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 9 August – Late in the day, Erdoğan in a speech called upon supporters not to pay heed to "various campaigns under way against Turkey", adding: "If they have dollars, we have our people, our righteousness and our God."<ref name=Allah /> As these remarks reduced markets' hope that the Turkish government were willing to tighten monetary policy or begin economic reform, throughout the night and into the next morning, the lira in a dramatic fall lost almost 10 percent of its value, touching the mark of 6 lira for a US dollar.<ref name=Allah />
* 14 August – Erdoğan announced a policy of boycott of US electronic products.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/aug/14/erdogan-turkey-boycott-us-lira-trump-pastor-brunson |title=Erdoğan says Turkey will boycott US electronic products |date=14 August 2018 |work=The Guardian|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=8 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180908055653/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/aug/14/erdogan-turkey-boycott-us-lira-trump-pastor-brunson|url-status=live}}</ref> On the same day, Turkey's banking regulator placed comprehensive limits on use of credit card instalments.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/credit-cards/turkish-banking-regulator-limits-credit-card-spending |title=Turkish banking regulator limits credit card spending |date=14 August 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=15 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180815024717/https://ahvalnews.com/credit-cards/turkish-banking-regulator-limits-credit-card-spending|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 15 August – [[Qatar]] pledged to invest $15 billion in Turkey making lira rally by 6%.<ref name="theguardian.com">{{Cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2018/aug/15/turkish-lira-rallies-as-ankara-increases-tariffs-on-us-imports |title=Turkish lira rallies as Qatar makes $15bn loan pledge |website=[[TheGuardian.com]] |date=15 August 2018|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=21 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421002659/https://www.theguardian.com/business/2018/aug/15/turkish-lira-rallies-as-ankara-increases-tariffs-on-us-imports|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="reuters.com">{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-currency-qatar-investments/qatar-to-invest-15-billion-in-turkey-source-says-banks-the-focus-idUSKBN1L01P7 |title=Qatar to invest $15 billion in Turkey; source says banks the focus |newspaper=Reuters |date=15 August 2018|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=30 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211230175342/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-currency-qatar-investments/qatar-to-invest-15-billion-in-turkey-source-says-banks-the-focus-idUSKBN1L01P7|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 16 August – The Turkish Statistical Institute reported that Turkey's industrial production declined by 2 percent in June from May, contracting for a second-straight month.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-manufacturing-growth-halves-lira-slump |title=Turkish manufacturing growth halves in lira slump |date=16 August 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=16 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180816194631/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-manufacturing-growth-halves-lira-slump|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 27 August – The Turkish Statistical Institute reported its economic confidence index dropping in August from 91.9 to 88.0, with another sharp drop in construction sector confidence leading the declines.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.turkstat.gov.tr/PreHaberBultenleri.do?id=27879 |title=Sectoral Confidence Indices, August 2018 |date=27 August 2018 |work=Turkish Statistical Institute|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=7 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200107111741/http://www.turkstat.gov.tr/PreHaberBultenleri.do?id=27879|url-status=live}}</ref>
*28 August – [[Moody's Investors Service|Moody's]] downgraded another 20 Turkish financial institutions.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-currency-banks/moodys-sounds-more-alarm-over-turkeys-banks-downgrades-20-firms-idUSKCN1LD1Z3 |title=Moody's sounds more alarm over Turkey's banks, downgrades 20 firms |author= |work=Reuters|access-date=13 September 2018 |language=en-US|archive-date=14 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190114075636/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-currency-banks/moodys-sounds-more-alarm-over-turkeys-banks-downgrades-20-firms-idUSKCN1LD1Z3|url-status=live}}</ref> The ratings agency estimated that Turkey's [[operating environment]] had "deteriorated beyond its previous expectations", and predicted that this deterioration would continue.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.moodys.com/research/Moodys-downgrades-20-financial-institutions-in-Turkey--PR_388052 |title=Moody's downgrades 20 financial institutions in Turkey |date=28 August 2018 |work=Moodys.com|access-date=13 September 2018|archive-date=19 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181019145408/https://www.moodys.com/research/Moodys-downgrades-20-financial-institutions-in-Turkey--PR_388052|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 29 August – Ownership of insolvent Turk Telekom transferred to "a joint venture of creditor banks."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/transfer-of-turk-telekoms-majority-stake-to-banks-approved-by-turkish-govt-136250 |title=Transfer of Türk Telekom's majority stake to banks approved by Turkish gov't |date=29 August 2018 |work=Hurriyet Daily News.|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=9 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181109150416/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/transfer-of-turk-telekoms-majority-stake-to-banks-approved-by-turkish-govt-136250|url-status=live}}</ref> Another measure of Turkish economic confidence slid from 92.2 in July to 83.9 in August, its lowest level since March 2009.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2018/08/29/traders-sell-lira-after-turkeys-economic-confidence-hits-9-year-low.html |title=Traders dump lira after Turkey's economic confidence hits a nine-year low |last=Reid |first=David |date=29 August 2018 |work=CNBC|access-date=13 September 2018|archive-date=2 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190302114615/https://www.cnbc.com/2018/08/29/traders-sell-lira-after-turkeys-economic-confidence-hits-9-year-low.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Research from consultancy [[Capital Economics]] indicated that Turkey has entered a 'steep' recession and predicted that the Turkish economy would contract by as much as 4% in the fourth quarter of 2018, before stagnating in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.businessinsider.fr/us/turkey-recession-capital-economics-2018-8 |title=Turkey has dived headfirst into a 'steep' and 'deep' recession |website=Business Insider France |language=fr-FR|access-date=13 September 2018|archive-date=13 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180913150458/http://www.businessinsider.fr/us/turkey-recession-capital-economics-2018-8|url-status=live}}</ref>
*30 August – Erkan Kilimci, the deputy governor of the Turkish central bank, resigned, putting further pressure on the lira, which fell almost 5% against the dollar throughout the day.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/turkey-cenbank-board/turkish-cenbanks-deputy-governor-kilimci-to-resign-sources-idUSL8N1VL3TI |title=Turkish cenbank's deputy governor Kilimci to resign – sources |agency=Reuters |work=U.S.|access-date=13 September 2018 |language=en-US|archive-date=13 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180913150237/https://www.reuters.com/article/turkey-cenbank-board/turkish-cenbanks-deputy-governor-kilimci-to-resign-sources-idUSL8N1VL3TI|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.gulf-times.com/story/604349/Turkish-lira-tumbles-another-5-as-deputy-bank-chie |title=Turkish lira tumbles another 5% as deputy bank chief quits |date=30 August 2018 |work=Gulf-Times|access-date=13 September 2018 |language=ar|archive-date=21 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180921081614/http://www.gulf-times.com/story/604349/Turkish-lira-tumbles-another-5-as-deputy-bank-chie|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://businessweekme.com/turkey-central-bank-deputy-governor-quits/ |title=Turkey Central Bank Deputy Governor Quits – Bloomberg Businessweek Middle East |website=businessweekme.com |language=en-US|access-date=13 September 2018|archive-date=13 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180913150326/http://businessweekme.com/turkey-central-bank-deputy-governor-quits/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*3 September – Turkey's central bank announced that inflation in August had risen to nearly 18 percent, a 15-year high.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/turkish-inflation-soars-fueling-fears-of-an-economic-crisis/4556659.html |title=Turkish Inflation Soars, Fueling Fears of Economic Crisis |last=Jones |first=Dorian |work=VOA|access-date=13 September 2018 |language=en|archive-date=20 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190220110938/https://www.voanews.com/a/turkish-inflation-soars-fueling-fears-of-an-economic-crisis/4556659.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
*10 September – Data released by the Turkish Statistical Institute showed a slowdown in Turkey's economic growth in the second quarter of 2018. The country saw a 5.2 percent increase in GDP in the June quarter, compared to 7.3 percent in the first quarter of the year.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/interestrates/turkey-gdp-growth-slows-in-q2-1027520250 |title=Turkey GDP Growth Slows in Q2 |work=Markets Insider|access-date=13 September 2018|archive-date=13 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180913150531/https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/interestrates/turkey-gdp-growth-slows-in-q2-1027520250|url-status=live}}</ref> Finance minister Berat Albayrak predicted that the economic slowdown would become more visible in the third quarter of 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-economy-gdp/turkish-economic-growth-dips-lira-crisis-darkens-outlook-idUSKCN1LQ0RD |title=Turkish economic growth dips, lira crisis darkens outlook |last=Kucukgocmen |first=Ali |work=U.S.|access-date=13 September 2018 |language=en-US|archive-date=23 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181123064148/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-economy-gdp/turkish-economic-growth-dips-lira-crisis-darkens-outlook-idUSKCN1LQ0RD|url-status=live}}</ref>
*12 September – Erdoğan sacked the entire management staff of Turkey's [[sovereign wealth fund]] and named himself chairman of the fund.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://asiatimes.com/article/erdogan-takes-wheel-of-turkish-wealth-fund/ |title=Erdogan takes wheel of Turkish wealth fund|access-date=13 September 2018 |language=en-US|archive-date=6 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306183327/https://asiatimes.com/2018/09/erdogan-takes-wheel-of-turkish-wealth-fund/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="bloomberg.com">{{Cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-09-12/erdogan-names-himself-chairman-of-turkey-wealth-fund-in-overhaul?srnd=premium-europe |title=Erdogan Names Himself Turkey Wealth Fund Chairman in Shakeup |newspaper=Bloomberg.com |date=12 September 2018 |access-date=13 September 2018|archive-date=13 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180913150338/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-09-12/erdogan-names-himself-chairman-of-turkey-wealth-fund-in-overhaul?srnd=premium-europe|url-status=live}}</ref> He also appointed Zafer Sonmez, formerly of Malaysia's government investment vehicle, as general manager.<ref name="bloomberg.com"/> Erdoğan's son-in-law [[Berat Albayrak]] was named as his deputy on the board of the sovereign wealth fund.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.ft.com/content/8fe07c16-b693-11e8-bbc3-ccd7de085ffe |title=Erdogan takes control of Turkey's sovereign wealth fund |website=Financial Times |date=12 September 2018 |language=en-GB|access-date=13 September 2018|archive-date=26 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190926050136/https://www.ft.com/content/8fe07c16-b693-11e8-bbc3-ccd7de085ffe|url-status=live}}</ref>
*13 September – Erdoğan published an executive decree requiring all contracts between two Turkish entities to be made in lira. The measure took effect immediately and requires existing contracts to be reindexed to the lira within 30 days.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-09-13/turkey-bans-fx-based-contracts-for-some-sales-leasing-rentals?srnd=premium-europe |title=Erdogan Publishes Decree Forcing Contracts in Turkey to Be Made in Liras |newspaper=Bloomberg.com |date=13 September 2018 |access-date=13 September 2018|archive-date=13 September During a speech in Ankara, Erdoğan sharply criticized the Turkish central bank and urged the bank to cut interest rates.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-09-13/turkey-bans-fx-based-contracts-for-some-sales-leasing-rentals?srnd=premium-europe |title=Erdogan Dollar Ban Sows Confusion Ahead of Key Rate Decision |newspaper=Bloomberg.com |date=13 September 2018 |access-date=13 September 2018|archive-date=13 September news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-09-13/turkey-s-erdogan-bashes-central-bank-hours-before-rates-decision?srnd=premium-europe |title=Turkey's Erdogan Bashes Central Bank Hours Before Rates Decision |newspaper=Bloomberg.com |date=13 September 2018|access-date=13 September 2018|archive-date=13 September Instead, the central bank sharply increased its benchmark lending rate, from 17.75 percent to 24 percent, beating Reuters' predictions of a hike to 22 percent.<ref>{{Cite news === Timeline of events (2019) ===
* 3 January: Inflation data showed continued high levels, prompting concerns about economic stability.
* 31 January: The Turkish government announced new measures to stabilize the lira.
* 22 March 2019: The government restricted foreign exchange transactions ahead of local elections.
* 31 March: Local elections took place, with economic concerns influencing voter sentiment.
* 6 June 2019: President Erdoğan dismissed the central bank governor, raising fears of political interference.
* 25 June: The Turkish lira experienced sharp volatility following the dismissal.
* 25 July 2019: The new central bank governor cut interest rates significantly, aiming to boost growth.
* 12 September 2019: Inflation showed signs of decline, but economic uncertainty persisted.
* 30 December 2019: The Turkish economy showed slight recovery, but concerns remained over long-term stability.

*16-17 December - Under Erdoğan's pressure, the CBRT cut its interest rate again, by 100 basis points, despite warnings not to do so, which made lira fall by 5.6%, to 15.689 TRY to the US dollar.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Erkoyun |first1=Ezgi |last2=Devranoglu |first2=Nevzat |date=2021-12-16 |title=Turkish lira hits new low after Erdogan's latest rate cut |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/currencies/turkish-lira-flat-ahead-cenbank-meeting-2021-12-16/|access-date=2021-12-20|archive-date=27 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220127014831/https://www.reuters.com/markets/currencies/turkish-lira-flat-ahead-cenbank-meeting-2021-12-16/|url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, the [[Borsa Istanbul|BIST 100]] index fell by a total of 8% during the trading day, triggering a [[Circuit breaker (trading)|circuit breaker]] on the stock exchange. The lira fell almost 7% that day, touching the 17 TRY/USD mark.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Stubbington |first1=Tommy |last2=Samson |first2=Adam |date=2021-12-17 |title=Turkey suspends stock trading as currency strain spreads through markets |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/e564829f-d381-4482-8dcb-100c6b9f8a0f|access-date=2021-12-20|archive-date=1 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220101060004/https://www.ft.com/content/e564829f-d381-4482-8dcb-100c6b9f8a0f|url-status=live}}</ref>
*20 December - Erdoğan doubled down on his ultra-loose monetary policy by citing the [[usury]] doctrine (which prohibits lending with interest) and insisting that the bank would not stop cutting its interest rates, prompting another currency selloff and plunging the lira to about 17.60 to the US dollar.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Erkoyun |first1=Ezgi |last2=Devranoglu |first2=Nevzat |date=2021-12-20 |title=Lira skids to new low after Erdogan cites Islamic usury |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/currencies/turkish-lira-near-record-low-erdogan-defends-low-rates-2021-12-20/|access-date=2021-12-20|archive-date=21 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121111730/https://www.reuters.com/markets/currencies/turkish-lira-near-record-low-erdogan-defends-low-rates-2021-12-20/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Pitel |first=Laura |date=2021-12-20 |title=Turkish lira resumes slide as Erdogan vows 'no going back' on rate cuts |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/1a365ce5-8921-4721-a18a-8b8bfcfd2786|access-date=2021-12-20|archive-date=24 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211224200530/https://www.ft.com/content/1a365ce5-8921-4721-a18a-8b8bfcfd2786|url-status=live}}</ref> The currency lost 58% of the value from the beginning of the year up to that date.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Ant |first1=Onur |last2=Kozok |first2=Firat |date=2021-12-20 |title=Lira Slides After Erdogan Says Islam Demands Lower Rates |work=Bloomberg |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-12-19/turkey-s-erdogan-says-islam-demands-lower-rates-and-so-does-he|access-date=2021-12-20|archive-date=22 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220122120641/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-12-19/turkey-s-erdogan-says-islam-demands-lower-rates-and-so-does-he|url-status=live}}</ref> The lira dropped to an all-time low of 18.36 TRY to the dollar but Erdoğan stepped in, announcing measures designed to protect lira-denominated deposits and to encourage converting foreign exchange deposits to liras. The market reacted immediately, moving the Turkish currency to ca. 13.50 liras/USD, after peaking at about 12.30, in what was the widest swing in the exchange rate since 1983.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Langley |first=William |date=2021-11-22 |title=Turkish lira holds on to gains after week's see-saw ride |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/afe6308a-e26b-40a5-ae7b-75939b232b93|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=30 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211230034756/https://www.ft.com/content/afe6308a-e26b-40a5-ae7b-75939b232b93|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Wong |first1=Marcus |last2=Vizcaino |first2=Maria Elena |last3=Ozsoy |first3=Tugce |date=2021-12-22 |title=Turkish Lira Swings After Its Biggest Rally in 38 Years |work=Bloomberg |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-12-20/lira-rebounds-from-record-low-as-erdogan-reveals-latest-plans|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=3 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220103130709/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-12-20/lira-rebounds-from-record-low-as-erdogan-reveals-latest-plans|url-status=live}}</ref>
*21 December - frenetic trading continues, with the exchange rate dropping to 11.0935 per dollar before going up to about 12.90 later in the morning and 12.50 by the afternoon.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Turak |first=Natasha |date=2021-12-21 |title=Turkish lira whipsaws from historic low after Erdogan announces rescue plan |work=CNBC |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/12/21/turkish-lira-whipsaws-from-historic-low-after-erdogan-announces-rescue-plan-.html|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=25 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220125031131/https://www.cnbc.com/2021/12/21/turkish-lira-whipsaws-from-historic-low-after-erdogan-announces-rescue-plan-.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Despite lira's gains, its strength is still severely diminished since January 2021, when 7.40 liras was enough to buy a US dollar.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Żuławiński |first=Michał |date=2021-12-21 |title=Potężne umocnienie tureckiej liry. Erdogan ma plan walki z dolaryzacją |url=https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/Potezne-umocnienie-tureckiej-liry-Erdogan-ma-plan-walki-z-dolaryzacja-8247075.html|access-date=2021-12-22 |website=Bankier.pl |language=pl|archive-date=22 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222085852/https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/Potezne-umocnienie-tureckiej-liry-Erdogan-ma-plan-walki-z-dolaryzacja-8247075.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
*23 December - amid continued optimism related to the new economic plan and as the state banks have poured almost $7 billion during the week preceding 23 December to stabilise the currency, the USD/TRY exchange rate falls another 10% to oscillate around 11 lira to the US dollar.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-12-23 |title=Lira extends rally in wake of Turkey's rescue plan |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/rates-bonds/lira-extends-rally-wake-turkeys-rescue-plan-2021-12-23/|access-date=2021-12-23|archive-date=23 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211223151201/https://www.reuters.com/markets/rates-bonds/lira-extends-rally-wake-turkeys-rescue-plan-2021-12-23/|url-status=live}}</ref> The lira hit 10.5343 to the dollar mark during trading,<ref name=":1055"/> strengthening by 40% since 20 December.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Turkish lira continues rebound following gov't measures - Latest News |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-lira-continues-rebound-following-govt-measures-170293|access-date=2021-12-23 |website=Hürriyet Daily News |date=23 December 2021 |language=en|archive-date=23 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211223151209/https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-lira-continues-rebound-following-govt-measures-170293|url-status=live}}</ref> Investors, however, brace for more volatility as the Borsa Istanbul 100 index tumbles.<ref name=":1055">{{Cite web |title=Turkey stock investors brace for more volatility as lira rallies |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/12/23/bbturkey-stock-investors-brace-for-more-volatility-as-lira-rallie|access-date=2021-12-23 |website=www.aljazeera.com |language=en|archive-date=26 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126224405/https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/12/23/bbturkey-stock-investors-brace-for-more-volatility-as-lira-rallie|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Timeline of events (2022) ===

* 4 July - Annual rate of inflation from June 2021 to June 2022 is reported to have reached 78.6%, with food prices doubling and transport costs increasing 123%. Since the beginning of the year, the Turkish lira has lost 20% of its value against the US dollar.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inflation soars to nearly 80% in Turkey as food prices double |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/07/04/economy/turkey-inflation-food-energy/index.html |date=2022-07-04 |last1=Cooban |first1=Anna |last2=Sariyuce |first2=Isil|access-date=2022-07-05 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref>

=== Timeline of events (2023) ===
* In 2023, Erdoğan began to follow orthodox banking methods. Under the guidance of [[Mehmet Şimşek]] and [[Hafize Gaye Erkan]], the central bank began to rapidly increase interest rates. By the end of the year, the interest rate stood at 42.5%,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/en/tcmb+en/main+menu/announcements/press+releases/2023/ano2023-51|title=Press Release on Interest Rates (2023-51)|date=21 December 2023|via=Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye}}</ref> and the annual inflation rate decreased to 53.86%.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.macrotrends.net/global-metrics/countries/tur/turkey/inflation-rate-cpi|title=Turkey Inflation Rate 1960-2024|via=Macrotrends}}</ref>

=== Timeline of events (2024) ===
* March - The central bank increased the interest rate to 50% under [[Fatih Karahan]], the new governor.<ref name="Interest rate unchanged">{{Cite web|url=https://www.euronews.com/business/2024/11/21/central-bank-of-turkey-keeps-key-interest-rate-unchanged|title=Central Bank of Turkey keeps key interest rate unchanged|via=Euronews|first=Indrabati|last=Lahiri|date=21 November 2024 }}</ref>
* 9 June - The [[Turkish Statistical Institute]] reports that the inflation rate of consumer prices rose 75.45% in May 2024, 3.37% on a monthly basis and up from 69.8% in April 2024. The steepest inflation rates were in education at 104.8%, housing at 93.2%, and hotels, cafes and restaurants at 92.9%. [[Capital Economics]] initially predicted that Turkish inflation would peak at 75%, but the higher rate of monthly inflation increase compared to both March and April made that prediction less certain.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Turak |first=Natasha |date=2024-06-03 |title=Turkey's inflation passes 75% in what economists believe is peak |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2024/06/03/turkeys-inflation-passes-75percent-in-what-economists-believe-is-peak.html |access-date=2024-06-10 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref>
* November - Inflation decreased to 47.09%.<ref name="November 2024 inflation">{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/EN/TCMB+EN/Main+Menu/Statistics/Inflation+Data/Consumer+Prices|title=Consumer Prices|via=Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye}}</ref> Interest rates kept as 50% for eight consecutive months.<ref name="Interest rate unchanged" />

== International consequences ==
{{See also|Turkey–European Union relations|Turkey–United States relations}}
{{Update|timelines|date=August 2024}}
The crisis has brought considerable risks of [[financial contagion]]. One aspect concerns risk to foreign lenders, where according to the [[Bank for International Settlements]], international banks had outstanding loans of $224 billion to Turkish borrowers, including $83 billion from banks in Spain, $35 billion from banks in France, $18 billion from banks in Italy, $17 billion each from banks in the United States and in the United Kingdom, and $13 billion from banks in Germany.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://turkey.theglobepost.com/turkey-economy-bonds-erdogan/ |title=Turkey's Economy Under Great Stress After Erdogan's Monetary Remarks |date=22 May 2018 |work=The Globe Post|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180712225655/http://turkey.theglobepost.com/turkey-economy-bonds-erdogan/|archive-date=12 July 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.welt.de/wirtschaft/article176765162/Drohende-Kreditausfaelle-Europas-Banken-fuerchten-tuerkischen-Kollaps.html |title=Europas Banken fürchten den türkischen Kollaps |date=29 May 2018 |newspaper=Die Welt |language=de |last1=Zschäpitz |first1=Holger|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=19 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180819191924/https://www.welt.de/wirtschaft/article176765162/Drohende-Kreditausfaelle-Europas-Banken-fuerchten-tuerkischen-Kollaps.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Another aspect concerns the situation of other [[emerging economies]] with high levels of debt denominated in USD or EUR, with respect to which Turkey may either be considered "a canary in the coalmine" or even by its crisis and the bad handling thereof increase international investors' retreat for increased perception of risk in such countries.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/indepth/opinion/turkey-lira-turmoil-herald-global-financial-crisis-180825165156035.html |title=Turkey's lira turmoil could herald a global financial crisis |date=26 August 2018 |publisher=Al Jazeera|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=19 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200919042156/https://www.aljazeera.com/indepth/opinion/turkey-lira-turmoil-herald-global-financial-crisis-180825165156035.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On 31 May 2018, the Institute of Financial Research (IIF) reported that the Turkish crisis has already spread to [[Lebanon]], [[Colombia]] and [[South Africa]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.businessinsider.nl/debt-contagion-in-argentina-and-turkey-is-spreading-to-other-countries-2018-6/?international=true&r=UK |title=Debt 'contagion' in Argentina and Turkey is spreading to other countries |date=6 June 2018 |publisher=Businessinsider |language=en|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612162245/https://www.businessinsider.nl/debt-contagion-in-argentina-and-turkey-is-spreading-to-other-countries-2018-6/?international=true&r=UK|url-status=live}}</ref> The fall of the value of the lira has also impoverished the inhabitants in northern [[Syria]], who use the lira for everyday transactions,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-12-12 |title=Turkish lira collapse piles misery on northern Syria |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211212-turkish-lira-collapse-piles-misery-on-northern-syria|access-date=2021-12-20 |website=France 24 |language=en|archive-date=5 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220105215128/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211212-turkish-lira-collapse-piles-misery-on-northern-syria|url-status=live}}</ref> and impacted the [[hazelnut]] industry hard, which is economically important in the country and produces 70% of world's hazelnuts.<ref>{{Cite news |author1=Jared Malsin |author2=Ahmed Deeb |date=2021-12-20 |title=Turkey's Currency Crisis Slams the Nutella Global Supply Chain |language=en-US |work=Wall Street Journal |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/turkeys-currency-crisis-slams-the-nutella-global-supply-chain-11639996201|access-date=2021-12-22 |issn=0099-9660|archive-date=27 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220127074016/https://www.wsj.com/articles/turkeys-currency-crisis-slams-the-nutella-global-supply-chain-11639996201|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Timeline of events (2018) ===

* 19 January – [[Fitch Ratings]] closed its [[Istanbul]] office after Erdoğan made numerous negative comments about [[credit rating agencies]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Why has rating agency Fitch left Turkey? |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/opinion/ugur-gurses/why-has-rating-agency-fitch-left-turkey-126075 |publisher=Hurriyet Daily News |date=22 January 2018|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=27 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180527023737/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/opinion/ugur-gurses/why-has-rating-agency-fitch-left-turkey-126075|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=e101 />
* 7 March – Credit ratings agency [[Moody's Investors Service]] downgraded Turkey's [[sovereign debt]], warning of an erosion of checks and balances under Erdoğan, and saying that the [[Turkish military operation in Afrin]], having strained [[Turkey–United States relations|ties with Washington]] and drawn the country deeper into the Syrian civil war, had added an extra layer of geopolitical risk.<ref>{{cite web |title=Moody's downgrades Turkish debt |url=https://www.ft.com/content/18004182-2263-11e8-9a70-08f715791301 |work=Financial Times |date=8 March 2018|access-date=23 May 2018|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612140317/https://www.ft.com/content/18004182-2263-11e8-9a70-08f715791301|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 1 May – Credit ratings agency [[Standard & Poor's]] cut Turkey's debt rating further into junk territory, citing widening concern about the outlook for inflation amid a sell-off in the Turkish lira currency.<ref>{{cite news |title=S&P cuts Turkey's rating deeper into 'junk' |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/turkey-ratings/update-1-sp-cuts-turkeys-rating-deeper-into-junk-idUSL8N1S85JM |work=Reuters |date=1 May 2018|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=2 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702034116/https://www.reuters.com/article/turkey-ratings/update-1-sp-cuts-turkeys-rating-deeper-into-junk-idUSL8N1S85JM|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 22 May – Turkish government dollar bonds traded at prices lower than those of [[Senegal]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/storm-turkeys-economy-bonds-trade-below-senegals |title=Storm in Turkey's economy as bonds trade below Senegal's |date=22 May 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=13 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613164010/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/storm-turkeys-economy-bonds-trade-below-senegals|url-status=dead}}</ref> On the same day, the [[Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus]] (TRNC) government started discussing abandonment of the Turkish lira for another currency.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/turkish-cypriots-consider-abandoning-sinking-lira |title=Turkish Cypriots consider abandoning sinking lira |date=22 May 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=7 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180707035437/https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/turkish-cypriots-consider-abandoning-sinking-lira|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 23 May – the [[Central Bank of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus]] discontinues offering loans to their citizens unless their salary is paid in a foreign currency.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews2.com/trnc/turkish-cyprus-bans-foreign-currency-personal-loans |title=Turkish Cyprus bans foreign currency personal loans |date=23 May 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=1 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612144816/https://ahvalnews2.com/trnc/turkish-cyprus-bans-foreign-currency-personal-loans|archive-date=12 June 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 28 May – [[Jordan]] terminated its free-trade agreement with Turkey, which had lately seen Turkish exports to Jordan increase fivefold.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-jordan/jordan-end-turkish-free-trade-agreement |title=Jordan to end Turkish free trade agreement |date=28 May 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612142606/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-jordan/jordan-end-turkish-free-trade-agreement|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 30 May – Credit ratings agency [[Moody's Investors Service]] lowered its estimate for growth of the Turkish economy in 2018 from 4 percent to 2.5 percent and in 2019 from 3.5 percent to 2 percent.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-growth-forecast-almost-halved-moodys |title=Turkish growth forecast almost halved at Moody's |date=30 May 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=27 August 2018|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612142430/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/turkish-growth-forecast-almost-halved-moodys|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 6 June – Bloomberg reported that [[Astaldi]], an Italian multinational construction company, was poised to sell its stake in the flagship [[Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge]] project for $467 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-06-06/astaldi-bridge-stake-is-said-valued-up-to-467-million-by-bidder |title=Astaldi May Fetch More Than What It Needs in Istanbul Bridge Sale |date=6 June 2018 |publisher=Bloomberg|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612135854/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-06-06/astaldi-bridge-stake-is-said-valued-up-to-467-million-by-bidder|url-status=live}}</ref> The project had failed to meet projections, requiring Ankara to boost operators' revenue from treasury coffers,<ref name=selim>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/ekonomi/iste-kopru-gercekleri-40507240 |title=İşte köprü gerçekleri |date=2 July 2017 |work=Hurriyet |language=tr|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=20 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180620150736/http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/ekonomi/iste-kopru-gercekleri-40507240|url-status=live}}</ref> and since early 2018, the partners in the joint venture had sought restructuring of $2.3 billion of debt from creditors.<ref name=pile />
* 7 June – Credit ratings agency Moody's Investors Service downgraded the ratings of 17 Turkish banks, reasoning "that the operating environment in Turkey has deteriorated, with negative implications for the institutions' funding profile."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/moodys-takes-rating-actions-on-19-turkish-financial-institutions-132988 |title=Moody's takes rating actions on 19 Turkish financial institutions |date=8 June 2018 |publisher=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612164912/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/moodys-takes-rating-actions-on-19-turkish-financial-institutions-132988|url-status=live}}</ref> Also on 7 June, Moody's put eleven of Turkey's top companies under review, because their credit quality was correlated in varying degrees to the government in [[Ankara]]. The firms included [[Koç Holding]], Turkey's biggest industrial conglomerate, [[Doğuş Holding]], which has applied to banks to restructure some of its debt, and [[Turkish Airlines]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-business/top-turkish-firms-put-under-review-moodys |title=Top Turkish firms put under review by Moody's |date=7 June 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612141622/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-business/top-turkish-firms-put-under-review-moodys|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 18 June – Credit ratings agency [[Fitch Ratings]] lowered its estimate for growth of the Turkish economy in 2018 from 4.7 percent to 3.6 percent, citing reasons including an anticipated reduction in government stimulus.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/fitch-cuts-turkeys-growth-outlook |title=Fitch cuts Turkey's growth outlook |date=18 June 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=18 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618181228/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/fitch-cuts-turkeys-growth-outlook|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 26 June – The [[European Union]]'s [[General Affairs Council]] stated that "the Council notes that Turkey has been moving further away from the European Union. Turkey's [[Accession of Turkey to the European Union|accession negotiations]] have therefore effectively come to a standstill and no further chapters can be stated for opening or closing and no further work towards the modernisation of the [[European Union–Turkey Customs Union|EU-Turkey Customs Union]] is foreseen."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cyprus-mail.com/2018/06/26/eu-council-issues-strong-message-about-turkeys-obligations/ |title=EU Council issues strong message about Turkey's obligations |date=26 June 2018 |work=Cyprus Mail|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=7 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200407070648/https://cyprus-mail.com/2018/06/26/eu-council-issues-strong-message-about-turkeys-obligations/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.zeit.de/politik/ausland/2018-06/recep-tayyip-erdogan-wahl-eu-zollunion-erklaerung |title=EU will Zollunion mit der Türkei nicht ausbauen |date=27 June 2018 |newspaper=Die Zeit |language=de|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=25 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191025123821/https://www.zeit.de/politik/ausland/2018-06/recep-tayyip-erdogan-wahl-eu-zollunion-erklaerung|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 13 July – Credit ratings agency Fitch Ratings downgraded Turkey's debt rating further into junk with negative outlook, reasoning that "economic policy credibility has deteriorated in recent months and initial policy actions following elections in June have heightened uncertainty (...) Monetary policy credibility has been damaged by comments by President Erdoğan suggesting a greater role of the presidency in setting monetary policy after the elections (...) Monetary policy has persistently been unable to bring inflation near its 5% target and inflation expectations have become unanchored. Key figures from the previous administration with reformist credentials were excluded from a new cabinet, appointed on 9 July, while the son-in-law of the president was appointed as Minister of Treasury and Finance."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/fitch-downgrades-turkey-bb-outlook-negative |title=Fitch Downgrades Turkey to 'BB'; Outlook Negative |date=13 July 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=14 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180714164402/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/fitch-downgrades-turkey-bb-outlook-negative|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 20 July – The government of Germany lifted export credit guarantee sanctions against Turkey, which it had implemented a year earlier in order to protest the ongoing state of emergency (OHAL) in Turkey and to effect the release of German citizen [[Deniz Yücel]] and others held under arrest by the Turkish government, after the German citizens concerned were freed and the state of emergency was lifted.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.handelsblatt.com/politik/international/export-absicherung-bundesregierung-hebt-obergrenzen-fuer-tuerkei-buergschaften-auf/22829208.html |title=Bundesregierung hebt Obergrenzen für Türkei-Bürgschaften auf |date=21 July 2018 |publisher=Handelsblatt |language=de|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=30 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220130023201/https://www.handelsblatt.com/politik/international/export-absicherung-bundesregierung-hebt-obergrenzen-fuer-tuerkei-buergschaften-auf/22829208.html?ticket=ST-3517967-USCwMlpvSYwdefejvLmG-ap6|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.foreignaffairs.com/articles/europe/2018-07-30/how-save-us-turkey-relationship |title=How to Save the U.S.-Turkey Relationship |date=30 July 2018 |journal=Foreign Affairs |author=Amanda Sloat|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=21 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211221053700/https://www.foreignaffairs.com/articles/europe/2018-07-30/how-save-us-turkey-relationship|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 26 July – European rating agency Scope Ratings placed Turkey's BB+ sovereign ratings on review for downgrade, citing i) "Deterioration in Turkey's economic policy and governance framework both before and in following the June election, which weigh on the effectiveness and credibility of fiscal, monetary and structural economic policy management" alongside ii) "Increasing downside risks to Turkey's macroeconomic stability stemming from external vulnerabilities."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scoperatings.com/#search/research/detail/157333EN |title=Scope places Turkey's BB+ ratings under review for downgrade |date=26 July 2018 |publisher=Scope Ratings|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=19 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180819182240/https://www.scoperatings.com/#search/research/detail/157333EN|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 27 July – At their summit in Johannesburg between 25 and 27 July, [[BRICS]] countries rejected Erdoğan's desire for Turkey to join the bloc.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://eurasiantimes.com/brics-turkey/ |title=BRICS Rejects Full-Time Membership to Turkey; Ankara Dejected |date=30 July 2018 |work=The EurAsian Times|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=31 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180731123548/https://eurasiantimes.com/brics-turkey/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 10 August – The [[European Central Bank]] voiced increased concerns about the exposure of some of the [[Euro]] currency area's biggest lenders to Turkey – chiefly [[BBVA]], [[UniCredit]] and [[BNP Paribas]] – in light of the lira's dramatic fall.<ref name=Allah>{{cite web |url=https://www.ft.com/content/51311230-9be7-11e8-9702-5946bae86e6d |title=Turkish lira plunges as crisis mounts |date=10 August 2018 |work=Financial Times|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=9 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180909073742/https://www.ft.com/content/51311230-9be7-11e8-9702-5946bae86e6d|url-status=live}}</ref> On the same day, the US government started "a bullet a day" economic sanctions against Turkey, designed to effect the release of US citizen [[Andrew Brunson]] and 15 others, held under arrest (on charges described as a sham by U.S. officials) by the Turkish government; in a first step, US President Donald Trump announced a doubling of tariffs on Turkish steel and aluminum.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://twitter.com/realDonaldTrump/status/1027899286586109955 |title=I have just authorized a doubling of Tariffs on Steel and Aluminum with respect to Turkey as their currency, the Turkish Lira, slides rapidly downward against our very strong Dollar! Aluminum will now be 20% and Steel 50%. Our relations with Turkey are not good at this time! |first=Donald J. |last=Trump |date=10 August 2018|access-date=11 March 2019|archive-date=11 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190311075601/https://twitter.com/realdonaldtrump/status/1027899286586109955|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/turkish-turmoil-is-tied-to-pastors-fate-1533942854 |title=Turkish Turmoil Is Tied to Pastor's Fate |date=10 August 2018 |publisher=Wall Street Journal|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=13 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180913114924/https://www.wsj.com/articles/turkish-turmoil-is-tied-to-pastors-fate-1533942854|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 16 August – European rating agency Scope Ratings downgraded Turkey's sovereign ratings to BB− from BB+ and revised the Outlook to Negative, citing in the downgrade: i) "Deterioration in Turkey's economic policy predictability and credibility, in view of monetary, fiscal and structural economic policies inconsistent with the rebalancing of the economy onto a more sustainable path"; ii) "Accentuated macroeconomic imbalances"; and iii) "The impact of balance of payment weaknesses on modest levels of international reserves."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scoperatings.com/#search/research/detail/157475EN |title=Scope downgrades Turkey's credit rating to BB- from BB+ and changes Outlook to Negative |date=16 August 2018 |publisher=Scope Ratings|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=19 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180819182240/https://www.scoperatings.com/#search/research/detail/157475EN|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 17 August – Credit ratings agencies Standard & Poor's and Moody's downgraded Turkey's debt rating further into junk, down to B+ (S&P) and Ba3 (Moody's).<ref name=ft1>{{cite web |url=https://www.ft.com/content/9ed3b3e2-a25b-11e8-85da-eeb7a9ce36e4 |title=S&P, Moody's send Turkey deeper into junk territory |work=[[Financial Times]] |date=17 August 2018|access-date=19 August 2018|archive-date=16 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181116151112/https://www.ft.com/content/9ed3b3e2-a25b-11e8-85da-eeb7a9ce36e4|url-status=live}}</ref> S&P predicted a recession for 2019 and inflation to peak at 22% in 2018, before subsiding to below 20% by mid-2019.<ref name=ft1 /> Moody's said that the chances of a swift and positive resolution to Turkey's turmoil was becoming less likely thanks to the "further weakening of Turkey's public institutions and the related reduction in the predictability of Turkish policy making."<ref name=ft1 />

=== Timeline of events (2021) ===
*11 September - Moody's cuts the Turkish debt rating again, downgrading it to B2 (five grades below investment level) with a negative outlook.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Moody's warns of crisis as it cuts Turkey's debt rating |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2020/9/14/moodys-warns-of-crisis-as-it-cuts-turkeys-debt-rating|url-status=live|access-date=2021-12-20 |website=Bloomberg |language=en |via=Al Jazeera|archive-date=20 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220120014/https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2020/9/14/moodys-warns-of-crisis-as-it-cuts-turkeys-debt-rating}}</ref>
*2 December - Fitch Ratings affirmed its BB− credit rating but revised the outlook to negative, citing "premature monetary policy easing cycle."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-12-02 |title=Fitch Revises Turkey's Outlook to Negative; Affirms at 'BB-' |url=https://www.fitchratings.com/research/sovereigns/fitch-revises-turkey-outlook-to-negative-affirms-at-bb-02-12-2021|url-status=live|access-date=2021-12-20 |website=Fitch Ratings|archive-date=20 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220120012/https://www.fitchratings.com/research/sovereigns/fitch-revises-turkey-outlook-to-negative-affirms-at-bb-02-12-2021}}</ref>
*10 December - Standard & Poor's lowered its forecast from stable to negative, warning of a potential downgrade to Turkey's debt rating if the situation worsens.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-12-10 |title=S&P lowers Turkey outlook to negative, citing 'rising risks' |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211210-s-p-lowers-turkey-outlook-to-negative-citing-rising-risks|access-date=2021-12-20 |website=France 24 |language=en|archive-date=20 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220120014/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211210-s-p-lowers-turkey-outlook-to-negative-citing-rising-risks|url-status=live}}</ref>
*14 December - Due to the unpredictability of the currency value, the Swiss-based bank [[UBS]] decided to discontinue coverage of the USD/TRY pair for its clients and retracted all prior advice for investors in the area.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-12-14 |title=UBS chief investment office stops coverage of U.S. dollar-Turkish lira pair |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/funds/ubs-chief-investment-office-stops-coverage-us-dollar-turkish-lira-pair-2021-12-14/|access-date=2021-12-20|archive-date=11 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220111211232/https://www.reuters.com/markets/funds/ubs-chief-investment-office-stops-coverage-us-dollar-turkish-lira-pair-2021-12-14/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Improvements ==
On 15 August 2018, [[Qatar]] pledged to invest $15 billion in the Turkish economy making the lira rally by 6%.<ref name="reuters.com"/><ref name="theguardian.com"/>

On 29 November 2018, the Turkish lira hit a 4-month high in value against the [[US Dollar]]. It recovered from 7.0738 against the dollar to 5.17 on 29 November, an increase of 36.8%. Reuters also reported in a response to a poll that it expects the inflation to decrease for the November month. The reasons that were given are the positive exchanges, discounts on products and tax cuts.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nasdaq.com/article/turkish-cpi-expected-to-fall-from-15year-peak-in-november-poll-shows-20181129-00458 |title=Turkish CPI expected to fall from 15-year peak in November, poll shows |date=29 November 2018 |publisher=Nasdaq |language=en|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=30 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181130030510/https://www.nasdaq.com/article/turkish-cpi-expected-to-fall-from-15year-peak-in-november-poll-shows-20181129-00458|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Politics and corruption ==

=== Turkish government statements of a foreign plot ===
{{See also|Conspiracy theories in Turkey}}

From a background of a long history of promoting conspiracy theories by the Turkish government of Erdoğan and the AKP,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://foreignpolicy.com/2016/09/12/the-tin-foil-hats-are-out-in-turkey/ |title=The Tin-Foil Hats Are Out in Turkey |date=12 September 2016 |publisher=[[Foreign Policy]] |author=Mustafa Akyol|access-date=10 January 2017|archive-date=24 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190724131756/https://foreignpolicy.com/2016/09/12/the-tin-foil-hats-are-out-in-turkey/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/international/archive/2018/06/turkey-erdogan-election-kurds/563240/ |title=How Nietzsche Explains Turkey |date=21 June 2018 |publisher=[[The Atlantic]] |author=Selim Koru|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=21 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621221333/https://www.theatlantic.com/international/archive/2018/06/turkey-erdogan-election-kurds/563240/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.al-monitor.com/pulse/originals/2017/01/turkey-believes-all-terrorists-are-united-against-it.html |title=Why Turkish government pushes 'global conspiracy' narrative |date=9 January 2017 |publisher=[[Al-Monitor]] |author=Mustafa Akyol|access-date=10 January 2017|archive-date=10 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170110123306/http://www.al-monitor.com/pulse/originals/2017/01/turkey-believes-all-terrorists-are-united-against-it.html|url-status=live}}</ref> with the emergence of the financial crisis, members of the government have stated that the crisis were not attributable to the government's policies, but rather were the conspiratorial work of shadowy foreign actors, seeking to harm Turkey and deprive President Erdoğan of support.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ft.com/content/a9b3dc8a-5a6a-11e8-bdb7-f6677d2e1ce8 |title=Tumbling Turkish lira tests voters' support for Erdogan |date=18 May 2018 |work=Financial Times|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=7 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207184025/https://www.ft.com/content/a9b3dc8a-5a6a-11e8-bdb7-f6677d2e1ce8|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=e101 /> During the major lira sell-off on 23 May 2018, Turkey's energy minister, Erdoğan's son-in-law [[Berat Albayrak]], told the media that the recent sharp drop in the value of the lira was the result of the machinations of Turkey's enemies.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/berat-albayrak/currency-crisis-clear-operation-against-turkey-energy-minister |title=Currency crisis "clear operation" against Turkey – Energy minister |date=23 May 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=23 May 2018|archive-date=23 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180523181447/https://ahvalnews.com/berat-albayrak/currency-crisis-clear-operation-against-turkey-energy-minister|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 30 May 2018, foreign minister [[Mevlüt Çavuşoğlu]] said that the plunge of the lira would have been caused by an organized campaign masterminded abroad, adding that the conspiracy would include both "the interest rate lobby" and "some Muslim countries", which he however refused to name.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-fm-accuses-some-muslim-countries-for-trying-to-demolish-economy-132594 |title=Turkish FM accuses 'some Muslim countries' for trying 'to demolish economy' |date=30 May 2018 |work=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=19 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180719134816/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-fm-accuses-some-muslim-countries-for-trying-to-demolish-economy-132594|url-status=live}}</ref> At an election campaign rally in Istanbul on 11 June 2018, Erdoğan said that the recently published 7.4 percent GDP growth figure for the January to March period would demonstrate victory against what he called "conspirators" whom he blamed for May's heavy falls of the Turkish lira.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/erdogan-seizes-on-growth-figures-to-persuade-skeptical-public-/4434745.html |title=Erdogan Seizes on Growth Figures to Persuade Skeptical Public |date=11 June 2018 |work=VOA News|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=14 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180614172510/https://www.voanews.com/a/erdogan-seizes-on-growth-figures-to-persuade-skeptical-public-/4434745.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In August, Erdoğan started using the formula of "the world fighting an economic war against Turkey".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2018/08/08/turkeys-erdogan-says-hes-fighting-an-economic-war-hes-right-its-war-against-reality/ |title=Turkey is fighting an 'economic war'—against reality |date=8 August 2018 |newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=8 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180908195943/https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2018/08/08/turkeys-erdogan-says-hes-fighting-an-economic-war-hes-right-its-war-against-reality/|url-status=live}}</ref> Part of this idea likely had to do with a row with America regarding the case of U.S. citizen [[Andrew Brunson]], which had a deleterious effect on Turkey-U.S. relations. Alongside sanctions on specific government figures, [[tariffs]] were also used by both countries to create economic pressure. Vox describes it as a "[[trade war|trade spat]]".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kirby |first1=Jen |title=The US-Turkey trade spat, explained |url=https://www.vox.com/world/2018/8/15/17687928/turkey-united-states-tariffs-lira-andrew-brunson |access-date=15 August 2018 |work=Vox |publisher=Vox Media |date=15 August 2018 |archive-date=15 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180815212456/https://www.vox.com/world/2018/8/15/17687928/turkey-united-states-tariffs-lira-andrew-brunson |url-status=live}}</ref> Commentators such as Vox's Jen Kirby have pointed to the pivotal role Brunson's case plays in it.

A tariff on steel and other products was placed on Turkey by the United States. However, Sarah Sanders has described the American tariffs as related to "national defense",<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/international/us-tariffs-on-turkey-for-national-security-will-not-be-lifted-white-house-118081600095_1.html |title=US tariffs on Turkey for national security, will not be lifted: White House |agency=IANS |newspaper=Business Standard India |date=16 August 2018|access-date=11 March 2019 |archive-date=4 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004062436/https://www.business-standard.com/article/international/us-tariffs-on-turkey-for-national-security-will-not-be-lifted-white-house-118081600095_1.html|url-status=live}}</ref> and thus not changeable by circumstances, noting that only the sanctions would be lifted upon the release of Brunson.

Erdogan describes these tariffs as an "economic war" against Turkey.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-currency-erdogan-idUSKBN1KW08U |title=Turkey is a 'target of economic war', Erdogan says |newspaper=Reuters |date=11 August 2018|access-date=11 March 2019 |via=www.reuters.com|archive-date=21 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190321153127/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-currency-erdogan-idUSKBN1KW08U|url-status=live}}</ref>

In retaliation, Turkey announced tariffs on US products, including the iPhone.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/erdogan-wants-boycott-of-us-electronics/4527699.html |title=Erdogan Wants Boycott of US Electronics |website=VOA|date=14 August 2018 |access-date=11 March 2019|archive-date=28 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180828071143/https://www.voanews.com/a/erdogan-wants-boycott-of-us-electronics/4527699.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The tariffs by Turkey cover products such as American cars, and coal. At a White House Press conference, Sanders described these as "regrettable".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/white-house-condemns-turkey-s-tariffs-on-us-products/4530059.html |title=US Condemns Turkey's New 'Regrettable' Tariffs |website=VOA|date=15 August 2018 |access-date=11 March 2019|archive-date=28 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180828134303/https://www.voanews.com/a/white-house-condemns-turkey-s-tariffs-on-us-products/4530059.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Sanders said that the Turkish economic trouble was part of a long-term trend that was not related to any actions America did.

On 22 August 2018, [[John R. Bolton]], speaking to Reuters, said "the Turkish government made a big mistake in not releasing Pastor Brunson... [e]very day that goes by that mistake continues, this crisis could be over instantly if they did the right thing as a NATO ally, part of the West, and release pastor Brunson without condition."<ref name="Reuters Bolton economy">{{cite news |last1=Williams |first1=Dan |title=U.S.-Turkey crisis could end 'instantly' if pastor freed: Bolton |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-turkey-bolton-interview/us-turkey-crisis-could-end-instantly-if-pastor-freed-bolton-idUSKCN1L70A5 |access-date=28 August 2018 |work=Reuters |date=22 August 2018 |archive-date=23 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181223204141/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-USA-turkey-bolton-interview/us-turkey-crisis-could-end-instantly-if-pastor-freed-bolton-idUSKCN1L70A5 |url-status=live}}</ref> He went on to state that Turkey's membership in NATO was not as much of a major foreign policy issue for the US, but instead the American focus was on individuals that the United States said Turkey is holding for non-legitimate reasons. Bolton also expressed skepticism in regard to Qatar's attempts to infuse money in the Turkish economy.<ref name="Reuters Bolton economy" /> 
Erdogan spokesman Ibrahim Kalin, in a written statement, described these remarks as an admission that, contra Sanders, the American tariffs were, in fact, in relation to the Brunson case and proof that the US intended them to economically war against Turkey.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-currency-erdogan-nato-exclusiv-idUSKCN1L729I |title=Exclusive: Bolton remarks proof U.S. targeting Turkey in economic... |newspaper=Reuters |date=22 August 2018|access-date=11 March 2019 |via=www.reuters.com|archive-date=13 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413100744/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-currency-erdogan-nato-exclusiv-idUSKCN1L729I|url-status=live}}</ref>

According to a poll from April 2018, 42 percent of Turks, and 59 percent of Erdoğan's governing AKP voters, saw the decline in the lira as a plot by foreign powers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/forty-two-percent-turks-say-liras-drop-foreign-plot |title=Forty-two percent of Turks say lira's drop is foreign plot |date=18 May 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=21 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181021191617/https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-lira/forty-two-percent-turks-say-liras-drop-foreign-plot|url-status=dead}}</ref> In another poll from July, 36 percent of survey respondents said it the AKP government was most responsible for the depreciation of the Turkish lira, while 42 percent said it was foreign governments.<ref name=poll>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/monkey-cage/wp/2018/08/22/turkeys-currency-is-plummeting-heres-what-it-might-mean-for-president-erdogan/?noredirect=on |title=Will Turkey's currency crisis hurt Erdogan? Here's what a new poll shows. |date=23 August 2018 |newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=26 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826150237/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/monkey-cage/wp/2018/08/22/turkeys-currency-is-plummeting-heres-what-it-might-mean-for-president-erdogan/?noredirect=on|url-status=live}}</ref> This was said to be caused by [[Censorship in Turkey|the government's far-reaching control]] over [[Media of Turkey|the media]] via the fact that those respondents mostly reading alternative views in the Internet were more likely to see their own government responsible, at 47 percent, than foreign governments, at 34 percent.<ref name=poll />

[[File:Muharrem İnce cropped.jpg|thumb|upright|right|[[Muharrem İnce]] (pictured) and [[Meral Akşener]] vowed to restore integrity to economic institutions in Turkey.]]
[[File:Meral Akşener İYİ Party (cropped)1.jpg|thumb|right|[[Meral Akşener]], İYİ Party leader and presidential candidate, announcing her economic policies on 7 May.]]

=== Crisis as a topic in the June 2018 elections ===
{{Further|2018 Turkish general election}}

On 16 May, a day after president Erdoğan had unsettled markets during his visit to London by suggesting he would curb the independence of the [[Central Bank of Turkey]] after the election, [[Republican People's Party]] (CHP) presidential candidate [[Muharrem İnce]] and [[İyi Party|İYİ Party]] presidential candidate [[Meral Akşener]] both vowed to ensure the independence of the central bank if elected.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-election-chp/erdogans-policies-driving-turkey-to-the-edge-challenger-says-idUSKCN1IH2BO |title=Erdogan's policies driving Turkey to the edge, challenger says |date=16 May 2018 |work=Reuters|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=29 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180829104156/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-election-chp/erdogans-policies-driving-turkey-to-the-edge-challenger-says-idUSKCN1IH2BO|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/tired-driver-is-sending-turkeys-economy-over-cliff-edge-iyi-party-head-aksener-131932 |title='Tired driver' is sending Turkey's economy over cliff edge: İYİ Party head Akşener |date=16 May 2018 |work=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=11 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180711234834/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/tired-driver-is-sending-turkeys-economy-over-cliff-edge-iyi-party-head-aksener-131932|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/chp-presidential-candidate-muharrem-ince-vows-to-ensure-central-bank-independence-if-elected-131953 |title=CHP presidential candidate Muharrem İnce vows to ensure Central Bank independence if elected |date=17 May 2018 |work=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612143120/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/chp-presidential-candidate-muharrem-ince-vows-to-ensure-central-bank-independence-if-elected-131953|url-status=live}}</ref>

In a 26 May interview [[Muharrem İnce presidential campaign, 2018|on his campaign trail]], CHP presidential candidate Muharrem İnce said on economic policy that "the central bank can only halt the lira's slide temporarily by raising interest rates, because it's not the case that depreciation fundamentally stems from interest rates being too high or too low. So, the central bank will intervene, but the things that really need to be done are in the political and legal areas. Turkey needs to immediately be extricated from a political situation that breeds economic uncertainty, and its economy must be handled by independent and autonomous institutions. My economic team is ready, and we have been working together for a long time."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://ahvalnews.com/muharrem-ince/muharrem-ince-turkish-economy-needs-political-reform-exclusive |title=Muharrem İnce: Turkish economy needs political reform |date=26 May 2018 |newspaper=Ahval |last1=Doğan |first1=Zülfikar|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=26 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180526190934/https://ahvalnews.com/muharrem-ince/muharrem-ince-turkish-economy-needs-political-reform-exclusive|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In a nationwide survey conducted between 13 and 20 May, 45 percent saw the economy (including the steadily-dropping lira and unemployment) as the greatest challenge facing Turkey, with foreign policy at 18 percent, the justice system at 7 percent and terror and security at 5 percent.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://ahvalnews.com/economy/turkeys-biggest-problems-economy-unemployment-survey |title=Turkey's biggest problems economy, unemployment – survey |date=23 May 2018 |newspaper=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612144112/https://ahvalnews.com/economy/turkeys-biggest-problems-economy-unemployment-survey|url-status=dead}}</ref>

İYİ Party presidential candidate Meral Akşener, supported by a strong economic team led by former Central Bank Governor Durmuş Yılmaz,<ref name=bentley /> had on 7 May presented her party's economic program, saying that "we will purchase the debts from consumer loans, credit card and overdraft accounts of 4.5 million citizens whose debts are under legal supervision of banks or consumer financing companies and whose debts have been sold to collection companies as of 30 April 2018. It is our duty to help our citizens with this condition, as the state has helped big companies in difficult situations."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/iyi-party-chair-aksener-vows-to-restructure-8-billion-lira-debts-of-4-5-million-citizens-131472 |title=İYİ Party chair Akşener vows to restructure 8 billion-lira debts of 4.5 million citizens |date=7 May 2018 |publisher=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612142310/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/iyi-party-chair-aksener-vows-to-restructure-8-billion-lira-debts-of-4-5-million-citizens-131472|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 13 June, CHP leader [[Kemal Kılıçdaroğlu]] reiterated the opposition's view that the [[state of emergency]] in place since July 2016 were an impediment to Turkey's currency, investment and economy, vowing that it be lifted within 48 hours in case of an opposition victory in the elections.<ref name=kemal>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/chp-vows-to-lift-emergency-rule-48-hours-after-ince-takes-office-as-president-133206 |title=CHP vows to lift emergency rule 48 hours after İnce takes office as president |date=13 June 2018 |publisher=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=15 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615131022/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/chp-vows-to-lift-emergency-rule-48-hours-after-ince-takes-office-as-president-133206|url-status=live}}</ref> İYİ Party leader and presidential candidate Akşener had made the same vow on 18 May,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/i-will-lift-state-of-emergency-day-after-elections-if-elected-meral-aksener-132071 |title=I will lift state of emergency day after elections if elected: Meral Akşener |date=20 May 2018 |publisher=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=13 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613160329/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/i-will-lift-state-of-emergency-day-after-elections-if-elected-meral-aksener-132071|url-status=live}}</ref> while CHP presidential candidate İnce had said on 30 May: "Foreign countries do not trust Turkey, thus they do not invest in our country. When Turkey becomes a country of the rule law, foreign investors will invest thus the lira will gain value."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/emergency-rule-must-be-lifted-to-lure-foreign-investments-chp-candidate-ince-132605 |title=Emergency rule must be lifted to lure foreign investments: CHP candidate İnce |date=30 May 2018 |publisher=Hurriyet Daily News|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=13 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613160534/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/emergency-rule-must-be-lifted-to-lure-foreign-investments-chp-candidate-ince-132605|url-status=live}}</ref> Early June, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan had suggested in an interview that the issue of lifting the emergency rule would be discussed the elections, however asked back: "What's wrong with the state of emergency?"<ref name=kemal />

=== Statements of corruption and insider trading ===
{{see also|Corruption in Turkey|2013 corruption scandal in Turkey}}

In early April 2017, [[Peoples' Democratic Party (Turkey)|Peoples' Democratic Party]] (HDP) presidential candidate [[Selahattin Demirtaş]], writing in a letter from prison—where he had been held without conviction since 2016 on charges of inciting violence with words—<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/04/13/magazine/inside-turkeys-purge.html |title=Inside Turkey's Purge |date=13 April 2017 |publisher=The New York Times Magazine |author=Suzy Hansen|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=28 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190528193423/https://www.nytimes.com/2017/04/13/magazine/inside-turkeys-purge.html|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Selahattin Demirtaş presidential campaign, 2018|saying]] that "the biggest problem for the youth in Turkey is corruption which has accompanied AKP governance."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rudaw.net/english/kurdistan/09052018 |title=Presidential candidate Demirtas promises youth, women, pension reforms |date=9 May 2018 |publisher=Rudaw|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=15 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615032212/http://www.rudaw.net/english/kurdistan/09052018|url-status=live}}</ref>

In late May 2018, [[Republican People's Party]] (CHP) deputy chair Aykut Erdoğdu called on the Financial Crimes Investigation Board of Turkey (MASAK) to investigate exchange rate transactions made amid rapid decline and partial recovery in the value of the lira on 23 May, saying there was [[insider trading]] by market participants who knew of the 300 basis points interest rate hike by the Turkish central bank in advance.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-economy/opposition-demands-investigation-transactions-during-lira-slide |title=Opposition demands investigation of transactions during lira slide |date=25 May 2018 |publisher=Ahval|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=8 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180708193307/https://ahvalnews.com/turkish-economy/opposition-demands-investigation-transactions-during-lira-slide|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In early July 2018, Turkey's Capital Markets Board (SPK) announced that, until the end of August, share purchases on the [[Borsa Istanbul]] by people party to the relevant company's internal information, or by those close to them (insider trading), would not be subject to a stock market abuse directive. Amid a public outcry, it suspended the directive some days later, without giving a reason for the move.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-bourse-directive/turkish-financial-watchdog-suspends-stock-market-abuse-article-idUSKBN1K40EQ |title=Turkish financial watchdog suspends stock market abuse article |date=14 July 2018 |work=Reuters|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=9 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210309000738/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-bourse-directive/turkish-financial-watchdog-suspends-stock-market-abuse-article-idUSKBN1K40EQ|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=erosion>{{cite news |url=https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/political-control-oversight-bodies-erodes-trust-turkeys-economy |title=Political control of oversight bodies erodes trust in Turkey's economy |date=22 August 2018 |newspaper=Ahval |author=Zülfikar Doğan|access-date=30 January 2022|archive-date=22 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180822145613/https://ahvalnews.com/turkey-economy/political-control-oversight-bodies-erodes-trust-turkeys-economy|url-status=live}}</ref>
